resentismiä, tämä tuskin kiinnostaa ketään kolmen vuoden päästä. muutenkaan mielestäni ei wikipediaan tarvitse kirjoittaa ihmisistä tällaisia negatiivisia asioita.
value.claim_en: In November 2015, Alexander Stubb falsely claimed in parliament that 90 percent of expert opinions on the nominee register were positive when the actual figure was 10 percent.
value.claim_fi: Marraskuussa 2015 Alexander Stubb väitti virheellisesti eduskunnassa 90 prosentin hallintarekisteriä koskevista asiantuntijalausunnoista olevan myönteisiä, vaikka todellinen osuus oli kymmenen prosenttia.
value.narrative_en: Criticism of Alexander Stubb over the 2015 nominee register controversy
value.uncertainty_note: This appears to be a multi-edit diff combining anti-vandalism restoration, wording neutralization, and an addition containing loaded phrasing ('jäi kiinni valehtelusta'); the revert focused on whether the recent controversy belonged in the biography (content_dispute vs. pov_push).

value.what_changed_en: Prematurely updated the infobox and lead text to state that Sauli Niinistö became the current 12th President of Finland starting on 22 January 2012 (the evening of the first round of the presidential election), overwriting his previous Speaker of Parliament role. It was reverted with a note explaining that one becomes president only after taking the oath of office.
value.claim_en: Sauli Niinistö is the current 12th President of Finland starting from 22 January 2012.
value.claim_fi: Sauli Niinistö on nykyinen Suomen tasavallan 12. presidentti 22. tammikuuta 2012 alkaen.
value.historical_note_en: On 22 January 2012, only the first round of the 2012 Finnish presidential election took place; Sauli Niinistö won the second round on 5 February 2012 and took office on 1 March 2012.
value.uncertainty_note: Could also be viewed as a false_factual_claim or premature enthusiasm during election night, as 22 January 2012 was only the first round of voting, though it reads like an overeager editor misunderstanding election and inauguration rules rather than malicious fabrication.

value.what_changed_en: Re-inserted a detailed passage describing an opinion piece by psychiatrist Seppo Mäkinen in Suomenmaa that questioned Prime Minister Sanna Marin's political judgment and mental health (including her nighttime cleaning habits), along with the Finnish Medical Association's condemnation of the piece. The reverting editor removed it, stating that opinion pieces by individual writers are not valid sources.
evidence: [[Psykiatria]]n erikoislääkäri Seppo Mäkinen kritisoi lokakuussa 2021 voimakkaasti Marinin nopeita kannanvaihdoksia
kyseenalaisti tämän harkinta- ja arviointikyvyn sekä teki huolestuneita arvioita Marinin henkisestä terveydentilasta
Marin itse myöntää kokevansa syyllisyyttä ja häpeää sitä, että hän on [[Pakkomielle|pakkomielteinen]] siivooja
Yksittäisten kirjoittajien sepustukset eivät ole kelvollisia lähteitä.
value.claim_en: Psychiatrist Seppo Mäkinen publicly questioned Sanna Marin's political judgment and mental health based on her policy shifts and obsessive cleaning habits, drawing criticism from the Finnish Medical Association.
value.claim_fi: Psykiatrian erikoislääkäri Seppo Mäkinen kyseenalaisti julkisesti Sanna Marinin poliittisen harkintakyvyn ja henkisen terveydentilan hänen kannanvaihdostensa ja pakonomaisen siivoamisensa perusteella, mistä Lääkäriliitto arvosteli häntä.
value.narrative_en: Questioning Sanna Marin's competence and mental fitness for office
value.uncertainty_note: Could also be viewed as a content_dispute over undue weight and sourcing standards for biographies of living persons, though giving two paragraphs to a single doctor's condemned op-ed strongly pushes a negative point of view.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted vulgar insults, racial and homophobic slurs, keyboard mashing, and a 'Prostitution' category at the top of the article about Finnish President Tarja Halonen, alongside an obscene edit summary.

Replaced Kekkonen's name in the infobox with 'Aurinkoinen' ('Sunny One'), inserted a link to a parody 'Church of Urho Kaleva Kekkonen' webpage, and added repeated all-caps joke text meaning 'LIGHT SHINES FROM GREAT URKKI'S BALD HEAD!'.

In a bundled diff of two edits, one claimed that former Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen denied using the residence meal benefit (attaching this to an existing source actually about Päivi Lipponen), while the other softened a description of Sanna Marin's December 2021 nightclub controversy from "partying" ("juhlimassa") to "spending free time" ("viettämässä vapaa-aikaa") and added mitigating details with a news citation.
evidence: totesi, että hänen aikanaan etua ei ole käytetty
Toukokuun 2021 kohussa lähteessä ei mainita mitään Paavo Lipposen kommenttia.
value.claim_en: Former Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen stated that the residence meal benefit was not used during his term, and Sanna Marin spent free time out after being advised that her coronavirus exposure required no special measures.
value.claim_fi: Paavo Lipponen totesi, ettei ateriaetua käytetty hänen aikanaan, ja Sanna Marin oli viettämässä vapaa-aikaa saatuaan ohjeen, jonka mukaan koronavirusaltistuminen ei aiheuttanut erityistoimenpiteitä.
value.narrative_en: Softening criticism of Sanna Marin's December 2021 nightclub controversy
value.uncertainty_note: The revert rolled back edits by two different contributors at once: an unsourced/misattributed claim confusing Paavo Lipponen with Päivi Lipponen (fitting source_manipulation or good_faith_error), and a softening of the wording regarding Marin's nightclub visit (fitting pov_push or content_dispute).

value.what_changed_en: The editor merged content from the separate articles on the Finland–Soviet Union Society (Suomi-Neuvostoliitto-Seura, 1944–1991) and the 1940 Society for Peace and Friendship between Finland and the Soviet Union into the Finland–Russia Society article, inadvertently removing mention of the current chairman Heikki Talvitie. The edit was reverted because a community vote on whether to merge the articles was still in progress.
evidence: Artikkeliiin yhdistetty tiedot tyngästä Suomen ja Neuvostoliiton rauhan ja ystävyyden seura, ns. SNS I sekä artikkelista Suomi-Neuvostoliitto-Seura
Peruutettu omavaltainen yhdistäminen, äänestys on kesken
palautus, mm. tiedot puheenjohtajasta tuhottu ja paikalle kopioitu SNS-seuran tiedot
value.claim_en: The histories of the 1940 Society for Peace and Friendship between Finland and the Soviet Union and the 1944–1991 Finland–Soviet Union Society belong in the same article as their successor, the Finland–Russia Society.
value.claim_fi: Vuoden 1940 Suomen ja Neuvostoliiton rauhan ja ystävyyden seuran sekä vuosien 1944–1991 Suomi–Neuvostoliitto-Seuran historiat kuuluvat samaan artikkeliin niiden jatkajan Suomi–Venäjä-Seuran kanssa.
value.uncertainty_note: Could also be classified as good_faith_error because it bypassed an ongoing merge vote and accidentally lost information about the current chairman during the merge.

value.what_changed_en: Added Urho Kekkonen's two terms as Minister for Foreign Affairs (1952–1953 and 1954) to the infobox, shifted the numbering of his other ministerial posts, and adjusted links and wording regarding his electoral district and resignation. The edit was made during an edit war and reverted as block evasion ('eston kiertoa').
evidence: ONHAN SE NYT KUMMA: Kekkonen oli ulkoministerinä kahdesti.
value.claim_en: Urho Kekkonen served twice as Minister for Foreign Affairs of Finland, from 26 November 1952 to 9 July 1953 and from 5 May 1954 to 20 October 1954.
value.claim_fi: Urho Kekkonen toimi Suomen ulkoasiainministerinä kahdesti: 26.11.1952–9.7.1953 ja 5.5.1954–20.10.1954.
value.uncertainty_note: Although the factual addition about Kekkonen's foreign minister terms is historically accurate, the edit was reverted primarily due to block evasion ('eston kiertoa' by a known long-term abusive user 'WPK') and ongoing infobox formatting disputes rather than factual inaccuracy; 'other' (procedural block-evasion revert) could also apply.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced all mentions of the Social Democratic Party of Finland (SDP) and being a Social Democrat with the Communist Party of Finland (SKP) and being a Communist, including the article's category, while using a fake revert summary to disguise the edit.
value.claim_en: Tarja Halonen is a Communist politician who belonged to the Communist Party of Finland (SKP).
value.claim_fi: Tarja Halonen on kommunistinen poliitikko, joka kuului Suomen Kommunistiseen Puolueeseen (SKP).
value.narrative_en: Portraying Social Democrat President Tarja Halonen as a Communist
value.historical_note_en: Tarja Halonen was a longtime member and MP of the Social Democratic Party of Finland (SDP), not the Communist Party of Finland (SKP).
value.uncertainty_note: This is deliberate political trolling/vandalism disguised with a fake revert summary, so it sits right on the boundary between 'false_factual_claim' and 'vandalism'.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced Tarja Halonen's name with spoonerisms and mocking nicknames ('Harja Talonen', 'Mr. Harja Talonen', 'Tavja', 'Karja Talonen'), changed her title from 'President of the Republic of Finland' to 'Ruiner of the Republic of Finland', and inserted a vulgarity ('fucks into her office') into a citation description.

Replaced the 2018 infobox portrait of Alexander Stubb with his 2024 official presidential photograph. The edit was later reverted because the uploaded official photograph lacked a free copyright license suitable for Wikipedia (the diff data also bundles several intermediate vandalism reverts that occurred during the 55 days).
value.uncertainty_note: The provided diff aggregates multiple revisions over 55 days (including reverts of intermediate IP vandalism such as a false helicopter crash claim), but the specific edit targeted by the revert (22367129) only changed the infobox image.

value.what_changed_en: Removed a passage calling Lipponen an important EU visionary and inserted a new section titled 'Connections to the Stasi and the KGB' alleging intelligence cooperation, while reframing his Nord Stream consultancy to emphasize Kremlin-controlled Gazprom ownership and Ulf Sundqvist's fraud.
evidence: [[Alpo Rusi]]n ''Vasemmalta Ohi'' osoitti Lipposen ja [[DDR]]:n tiedustelupalvelun [[Stasi]]n välisen yhteistyö alkaneen vuonna 1969.
Lipposen arvellaan avustaneen Stasin lisäksi myös [[Neuvostoliitto|Neuvostoliiton]] [[KGB]]:tä.
value.claim_en: Paavo Lipponen collaborated with the East German Stasi and the Soviet KGB during the Cold War and later worked for Kremlin-controlled Gazprom interests.
value.claim_fi: Paavo Lipponen teki yhteistyötä DDR:n Stasin ja Neuvostoliiton KGB:n kanssa kylmän sodan aikana ja työskenteli myöhemmin Kremlin kontrolloiman Gazpromin etujen hyväksi.
value.narrative_en: Portraying Paavo Lipponen as a Cold War Soviet/East German intelligence collaborator and pro-Kremlin actor
value.uncertainty_note: The edit also selectively misrepresents cited sources (as noted in the revert summary pointing out that having a Stasi file or codename applied to Western politicians who were targets rather than collaborators) and introduces minor syntax errors like 'lähde}}{{', overlapping with source_manipulation.

value.what_changed_en: In a botched revert or copy-paste editing attempt, the editor tried to change capitalization (e.g., 'YYA' to 'Yya' and 'NATO' to 'Nato'), adjust wikilinks, and replace an irrelevant reference to a 1992 labor policy agreement with a statement on the 1992 termination of the FCMA treaty via an exchange of notes, while accidentally duplicating or scrambling large portions of the article.
evidence: Solmittaessa [[naapuruussopimus|sopimusta Suomen ja Venäjän suhteiden perusteista]] vuonna 1992 sovittiin yya-sopimuksen lopettamisesta Suomen ja [[Venäjä]]n keskinäisellä noottien vaihdolla
Suomi teki yhteistyösopimuksen [[1992]] Neuvostoliiton seuraajavaltion, [[Venäjän federaatio]]n kanssa työpolitiikan alalta
value.claim_en: When concluding the Treaty on the Foundations of Relations between Finland and Russia in 1992, it was agreed to terminate the Finno-Soviet Treaty through a mutual exchange of notes.
value.claim_fi: Solmittaessa sopimusta Suomen ja Venäjän suhteiden perusteista vuonna 1992 sovittiin yya-sopimuksen lopettamisesta Suomen ja Venäjän keskinäisellä noottien vaihdolla.
value.uncertainty_note: The diff shows mirrored blocks in removed and inserted text alongside multiple chained revert summaries, indicating either duplicated article text prior to/resulting from a botched revert or an ongoing style/orthography dispute ('YYA' vs 'Yya') mixed with a valid factual correction.

value.what_changed_en: The editor re-added a duplicated, unsourced mention of the Pudasjärvi UFO wave ('UFO sightings were reported from Pudasjärvi, the Pudasjärvi UFO wave'), altered phrasing ('Significant phenomenon' to 'Significant'), and introduced broken link markup and paragraph splits. The reverter rejected it as unsourced and unnecessary.
value.claim_en: UFO sightings in Pudasjärvi (the Pudasjärvi UFO wave) were reported in the news during the 1970s in Finland.
value.claim_fi: Pudasjärveltä uutisoitiin 1970-luvulla ufohavaintoja eli niin sanottu Pudasjärven ufo-aalto.
value.uncertainty_note: Because this edit reverts an earlier revert, it also borders on content_dispute, though the duplicated sentence, broken brackets, and lack of sources point primarily to an inept, undue-weight good-faith addition.

value.what_changed_en: Changed the spelling and punctuation of the Finland–Russia Society's name from 'Suomi–Venäjä-Seura' to 'Suomi-Venäjä-seura' throughout the text and citations, added a rename request template claiming the capital 'S' in 'seura' was dropped in 2019, and made minor wording and formatting adjustments (such as changing 'collapsed' to 'dissolved' regarding the Soviet Union, changing the website URL, and inadvertently breaking a wikilink). The edit was reverted as block evasion by a banned user ('WPK').
evidence: ja nykyiseksi vuonna 2019, kun isosta alkukirjaimesta seura-sanassa luovuttiin.
value.claim_en: The Finland–Russia Society dropped the capital letter in the word 'seura' ('society') in 2019, making its current spelling 'Suomi-Venäjä-seura'.
value.claim_fi: Suomi–Venäjä-Seura luopui sanan 'seura' isosta alkukirjaimesta vuonna 2019, jolloin sen kirjoitusasuksi tuli 'Suomi-Venäjä-seura'.
value.uncertainty_note: The edit was reverted explicitly for block evasion ('eston kiertoa (WPK)') rather than solely on content merits. Whether the society officially changed the capitalization in 2019 (versus the editor doing original research from a blog post and altering quoted source titles to match) could also support 'false_factual_claim' or 'other'.

value.what_changed_en: Added three repetitive sentences to the personal life section stating that Alexander Stubb was arrogant as a schoolboy and engaged in school bullying, citing three Helsingin Sanomat and Nyt links. The phrasing escalates from attributed interpretation to flatly stating he practiced bullying as a hobby ('harrasti koulukiusaamista'), and includes poorly formatted bare URLs and duplicate lines.
evidence: Stubin kerrotaan olleen koulupoikana ylimielinen ja hänen käytöstään on tulkittu myös koulukiusaamiseksi.
value.claim_en: Alexander Stubb was arrogant in his youth and engaged in school bullying.
value.claim_fi: Alexander Stubb oli nuoruudessaan ylimielinen ja syyllistyi koulukiusaamiseen.
value.narrative_en: Highlighting Alexander Stubb's admitted youth school bullying to portray him negatively
value.uncertainty_note: In spring 2014 Helsingin Sanomat did report on Stubb's youth bullying (which he acknowledged and apologized for), so the underlying topic is sourced; however, pasting three repetitive sentences escalating to loaded phrasing ('harrasti koulukiusaamista') shortly after he became Prime Minister points to POV pushing rather than a neutral good-faith addition.

value.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced sentence stating that the Finnish broadcast of the 1984 US television series 'V' was halted mid-run in the 1980s. The edit was reverted four days later as unsourced ('lähteetön').
evidence: 1980-luvulla yhdysvaltalainen televisiosarja '[[V (vuoden 1984 televisiosarja)|V]]':n esittäminen keskeytetiin Suomessa kesken sarjan.
value.claim_en: The Finnish broadcast of the 1984 American television series V was discontinued mid-series as an instance of censorship in the 1980s.
value.claim_fi: Yhdysvaltalaisen vuoden 1984 V-televisiosarjan esittäminen keskeytettiin Suomessa kesken sarjan sensuurin vuoksi 1980-luvulla.
value.uncertainty_note: MTV did notoriously stop airing V in Finland in 1986 after controversy over its perceived violence and scariness for children, though whether it constitutes official state censorship versus broadcaster self-regulation is debatable, and the addition lacked a citation.

value.what_changed_en: Added a poorly formatted, repetitive section describing the caricature of Paavo Lipponen in the animated political satire TV series 'Itse valtiaat', citing a Vimeo video. Reverted as trivial and belonging in the TV show's own article rather than the politician's biography.
evidence: , todella suuri ystävyys Sauli Niinistöön ja kahden pullan syöminen kerralla eduskuntatalon kahviossa
value.claim_en: Paavo Lipponen was portrayed as a character in the 2001–2008 political satire series Itse valtiaat with specific recurring gags and mannerisms.
value.claim_fi: Paavo Lipposesta oli hahmo vuosina 2001–2008 esitetyssä poliittisessa satiirisarjassa Itse valtiaat, jolla oli tiettyjä toistuvia vitsejä ja maneereja.
value.uncertainty_note: The inserted text contains a Vimeo URL that was created later than March 2014 (or the metadata combines multiple edits from the revert chain), though the nature of the edit as misplaced pop-culture trivia is completely clear.

value.what_changed_en: Removed the statement that Urho Kekkonen did not have a crofter (torppari) background, replacing it with assertions based on primary archival records (parish and tax registers) that his father rented Lepikon torppa as a crofter and never owned it, while also altering family genealogical details and fixing a dead link. An intermediate edit summary notes this was objected to as original research using primary sources to contradict secondary sources like the National Biography.
evidence: Vaikka Kekkosen [[Pielavesi|Pielavedellä]] sijaitseva syntymäkoti tunnetaan [[Lepikon torppa]]na, Kekkosella ei ole [[torppari]]taustaa.
Kuopion läänin henkikirjojen 1901-1905 mukaan Juho Kekkonen oli Pielaveden talon n:o 5 Niskalan torppari, eikä siten koskaan omistanut rakennusta
hän lisäsi osittain uutta tutkimusta (epämääräisesti viitaten ensisijaisiin lähteisiin ilman siteerausta) joka yrittää kumota luotettavia lähteitä
value.claim_en: Urho Kekkonen's father Juho Kekkonen was a crofter who rented rather than owned the family's birth home, and was the middle of three sons.
value.claim_fi: Urho Kekkosen isä Juho Kekkonen oli torppari, joka vuokrasi perheen syntymäkodin omistamisen sijaan, ja hän oli keskimmäinen kolmesta pojasta.
value.historical_note_en: Standard Finnish biographical historiography (such as Kansallisbiografia and Juhani Suomi's biographies) states that despite the later name 'Lepikon torppa', Juho Kekkonen bought the cottage rather than holding a crofter tenancy.
value.uncertainty_note: The edit data bundles multiple consecutive edits by different editors (an original research addition, a revert of that addition, a dead-link fix, and a final 'oops, wrong version' revert). Could equally be classified as content_dispute depending on whether the focus is the policy violation (WP:NOR) or the disagreement between editors.

value.what_changed_en: In a botched sequence of reverts and edits, the editor added Paavo Lipponen's 2012 presidential election result (6.7% of votes, fifth place) with a Yle reference, while accidentally breaking a `<ref>` tag and duplicating the 'Return to politics' section.
evidence: Käyttäjän [editor] (keskustelu) muokkaukset kumottiin ja sivu palautettiin viimeisimpään käyttäjän 80.220.x.x tekemään versioon.
value.claim_en: Paavo Lipponen received 6.7% of the votes and placed fifth in the 2012 Finnish presidential election.
value.claim_fi: Paavo Lipponen sai 6,7 % äänistä ja sijoittui viidenneksi vuoden 2012 presidentinvaaleissa.
value.uncertainty_note: The edit summary indicates a combined sequence of reverts (likely merged edits by the same user) that mangled the wikitext, so 'other' (tool/technical error) could also apply alongside 'good_faith_error'.

value.what_changed_en: Re-added a 'Recommended links' ('Suositeltavia linkkejä') section containing external links to a personal webpage justifying anti-Russian sentiment ('ryssäviha') and an activist group focused on Soviet and Russian genocide and war crimes, along with a meta-comment stating that the article specifically discusses Finnish anti-Russian hatred. This was part of an edit war over whether these partisan external links belonged in the article.
evidence: Tässä artikkelissa käsitellään nimenomaan suomalaisten ryssävihaa.
roskalinkit pois | palautus, katso muokkaushistoriasta perusteet.
value.claim_en: Partisan anti-Russian websites justifying hatred of Russia are recommended reading for the topic, which specifically concerns Finnish hatred of Russians.
value.claim_fi: Venäläisvihaa perustelevat sivustot ovat suositeltavaa luettavaa aiheesta, joka käsittelee nimenomaan suomalaisten ryssävihaa.
value.narrative_en: Promoting or illustrating Finnish anti-Russian sentiment
value.uncertainty_note: Without seeing the earlier edit history, it is slightly unclear whether the editor was promoting anti-Russian views ('Suositeltavia linkkejä' means 'Recommended links') or sincerely arguing in a content dispute that primary examples of Finnish anti-Russian sentiment should be linked in an article about the phenomenon.

value.what_changed_en: Rewrote a sentence on 1970s maritime transport, replacing the mention of growing passenger and freight volumes with an unsourced claim that 'maritime traffic became common' and adding details about early cruise ferries and GTS Finnjet. The reverter rejected the series of three edits as unsourced, poorly worded, and losing the mention of freight traffic.
evidence: lähteetön ja huono lisäys, joka hukkaa rahtiliikenteen. Meriliikenne ei yleistynyt, vaan matkustajalaivaliikenne.
value.claim_en: Maritime traffic became common in Finland in the 1970s with the introduction of the first cruise ferries, including GTS Finnjet, the largest and fastest car-passenger ferry of its time.
value.claim_fi: Meriliikenne yleistyi Suomessa 1970-luvulla ensimmäisten niin sanottujen risteilijä-alusten myötä, joista GTS Finnjet oli aikansa suurin ja nopein matkustaja-autolautta.
value.uncertainty_note: The diff appears to compare across three consecutive edits by the same editor (as indicated by the revert summary and GTS Finnjet text appearing in removed_text), making the exact intermediate steps slightly fragmented, though the overall good-faith intent is clear.

value.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced paragraph claiming that the Taistoist idealization of the Soviet system was exceptional among capitalist countries and attributing this to a lack of Soviet-critical literature in post-war Finland, claiming works by Viktor Kravchenko and Milovan Djilas were never translated into Finnish. The reverter removed it as a bold, unsourced claim.
evidence: Taistolaisuudelle tyypillinen Neuvostoliiton järjestelmän ihannointi oli poikkeus kapitalistisissa maissa.
eikä muualla suurta huomiota herättäneitä kirjoja koskaan julkaistu suomeksi, kuten Viktor Kravchenkon ''I chose freedom'' (1946) ja Milovan Djilasin ''Conversations with Stalin'' (1962).
rv, nyt on sellainen väite että kumoan lähteettömänä
value.claim_en: Taistoist idealization of the Soviet system was exceptional among capitalist countries because Soviet-critical literature—such as Kravchenko's 'I Chose Freedom' and Djilas's 'Conversations with Stalin'—was not published in Finnish after the Second World War.
value.claim_fi: Taistolaisuudelle tyypillinen Neuvostoliiton järjestelmän ihannointi oli poikkeus kapitalistisissa maissa, koska Suomessa ei sotien jälkeen julkaistu neuvostokriittistä kirjallisuutta, kuten Kravchenkon tai Djilasin teoksia.
value.narrative_en: Finlandization and post-war self-censorship explaining Finnish pro-Soviet radicalism
value.historical_note_en: Both cited books were in fact published in Finnish shortly after their original release: Viktor Kravchenko's 'Valitsin vapauden' in 1947 and Milovan Djilas's 'Keskusteluja Stalinin kanssa' in 1962.
value.uncertainty_note: The edit combines unsourced original-research causal analysis (fitting good_faith_error or pov_push) with demonstrably false bibliographic claims; it is unclear whether the editor was sincerely mistaken or pushing an ideological narrative about censorship.

value.what_changed_en: Made sweeping copyedits, stylistic changes, and additions across the article on the Finno-Soviet Treaty of 1948, including replacing the Swedish treaty name with the Russian transliteration, revising a 1973 photo caption from 'signing' to '25th anniversary', framing the Winter War's outbreak explicitly as a Soviet attack, and adding unsourced legalistic speculation that the treaty theoretically obliged the USSR to fight against its own potential attack on Finland (duplicated in two places). It was reverted as block evasion ('eston kiertoa').
evidence: Toisin sanoen, sopimuksen sotilasosan nojalla Neuvostoliiton olisi tarvittaessa pitänyt avustaa Suomea tai jopa taistella myös omaa mahdollista hyökkäystään vastaan.
Kielenä ei ruotsi, sillä sopimus tehtiin kahtena suomen- ja venäjänkielisenä kappaleena.
value.claim_en: Because East Germany was allied with the Soviet Union in the Warsaw Pact, the Finno-Soviet Treaty's clause against aggression by Germany or its allies technically obliged the Soviet Union to defend Finland even against a Soviet attack, and the treaty's official languages were only Finnish and Russian.
value.claim_fi: Koska Itä-Saksa oli Neuvostoliiton liittolainen Varsovan liitossa, YYA-sopimuksen Saksaa tai sen liittolaista koskeva pykälä velvoitti teknisesti Neuvostoliiton puolustamaan Suomea jopa sen omaa hyökkäystä vastaan, eikä ruotsi ollut sopimuksen kieli.
value.narrative_en: Anti-Soviet framing and legalistic reinterpretation of the Finno-Soviet Treaty
value.uncertainty_note: The edit mixes plausible factual corrections (e.g., the 1973 Finlandia Hall event vs. signing, original treaty languages), idiosyncratic style/spelling changes ('Iosif', typos like 'sijaint i' and 'Sopimusprosesiinn', duplicated paragraphs), unsourced original research, and sharper anti-Soviet phrasing ('hyökkäämällä Suomeen', 'kommunistijohtoista'), and was reverted purely due to block evasion by a known sockpuppeteer; 'good_faith_error', 'pov_push', or 'other' could also arguably apply.

value.what_changed_en: Added a paragraph claiming that a 2026 Supreme Court ruling restricting Päivi Räsänen's pamphlet on sexuality constituted the only book censorship of the 2000s in Finland, framed around threats to religious freedom and citing a podcast interview with Räsänen. The reverter removed it as non-neutral and poorly sourced, noting that reliable sources do not describe the ruling as book censorship.
evidence: 2000-luvun toistaiseksi ainoa kirjasensuuri annettiin 2026 Päivi Räsäsen "mieheksi ja naiseksi hän heidät loi"-pamfletille.
erityisesti johtuen osan toiveista ja toisten pelosta Raamatun sensurointia ja kristillistä uskonvapautta kohtaan.
Nimi=Päivi Räsänen paljastaa KAIKEN ensimmäisessä haastattelussa KKO:n päätöksen jälkeen
epäneutraalia, lähteenä podcast-jakso, asiallisemmissa lähteissä asiaa ei ole kuvattu kirjasensuurina.
value.claim_en: A 2026 Finnish Supreme Court order restricting parts of Päivi Räsänen's online pamphlet constitutes the only instance of book censorship in 21st-century Finland and prompted ministerial efforts to revise hate-speech laws.
value.claim_fi: Korkeimman oikeuden vuoden 2026 määräys rajoittaa Päivi Räsäsen pamfletin sisältöä on 2000-luvun ainoa kirjasensuuritapaus Suomessa ja johti ministerien haluun päivittää kiihottamispykälää.
value.narrative_en: Framing hate-speech rulings against conservative Christian views as state censorship and a threat to religious freedom
value.historical_note_en: Finland's statutory offense of agitation against a population group (kiihottaminen kansanryhmää vastaan) existed in the Criminal Code decades before Räsänen's 2004 pamphlet was published, contrary to the edit's claim that the pamphlet predated the provision.
value.uncertainty_note: Also contains factual errors (e.g., about when the hate-speech law was enacted) and relies on a partisan podcast source, overlapping with false_factual_claim and source_manipulation, though non-neutral framing as 'book censorship' is the overarching issue.

value.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced paragraph about suspicions of anti-Sovietism directed at Centre Party politicians outside the 'K-line' faction, mentioning the 1982 presidential primary between Johannes Virolainen and Soviet-favoured Ahti Karjalainen. The edit was reverted with the summary 'mielipiteet pois' ('opinions out').
evidence: Maalaisliitto/keskustapuolueessa neuvostovastaisuusepäilyjä esitettiin ajoittain [[K-linja|K-linjan]] ulkopuolisia keskustapoliitikkoja kohtaan.
vastakkain olivat [[Johannes Virolainen]] ja neuvostosuosiosta nauttinut [[Ahti Karjalainen]]
value.claim_en: Within the Agrarian League/Centre Party, politicians outside the K-line were occasionally suspected of anti-Sovietism, culminating in the party's 1982 presidential primary between Johannes Virolainen and the Soviet-favoured Ahti Karjalainen.
value.claim_fi: Maalaisliitto- ja keskustapuolueessa esitettiin ajoittain neuvostovastaisuusepäilyjä K-linjan ulkopuolisia poliitikkoja kohtaan, mikä kärjistyi vuoden 1982 presidenttiehdokasvalinnassa Johannes Virolaisen ja neuvostosuosiosta nauttineen Ahti Karjalaisen välillä.
value.uncertainty_note: The added text aligns broadly with mainstream Finnish political history regarding the 1981 Centre Party Kuopio party congress (Virolainen vs. Karjalainen and the 'idänkortti' / Soviet card), so it appears to be a sincere, unsourced addition rather than ideological spin, though the reverter dismissed it as opinion ('mielipiteet pois'), making 'pov_push' or 'content_dispute' secondary possibilities.

value.what_changed_en: Added a subsection titled "Kanava tunnukset" ("Channel idents", misspelled as two words instead of "Kanavatunnukset") containing an image gallery of logos for TV1, TV2, and MTV, including a 1983 TV1 logo in an article about the 1970s. The edit was reverted as unnecessary in this overview article and linguistically weak.
evidence: rv (turha tässä artikkelissa ja kielellisesti heikko)
value.claim_en: These logos represented the Finnish television broadcasters TV1, TV2, and MTV in the 1970s.
value.claim_fi: Nämä logot edustivat suomalaisia televisiotoimijoita TV1:tä, TV2:ta ja MTV:tä 1970-luvulla.

value.what_changed_en: Added a 'Links' ('Linkkejä') section containing an external link to Juhani Putkinen's personal homepage essay titled 'An analysis of the causes of hatred of Russians' ('Ryssävihan syiden erittelyä').
value.narrative_en: Justification of Finnish anti-Russian sentiment
value.uncertainty_note: Adding an external link to a partisan personal webpage overlaps between link spam ('other') and 'pov_push', as Juhani Putkinen's essays are known for strong nationalist and anti-Russian polemics; without the linked page's exact text in the diff, 'other' (link spam) is the most direct fit.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced the article's lead section and infobox with broken infobox fragments, profanity, repeated homophobic slurs ('PASKAAAAAAAAAAAAA' meaning 'shit', repeated 'HOMO', 'pieeeruuu' meaning 'fart'), and the exclamation 'URHO ON KOVA MIES!!!' ('Urho is a tough guy!!!').
value.uncertainty_note: The edit summary and diff appear to combine multiple consecutive edits or reverts in the dataset log, as the timestamp is 2007 while some inserted syntax ('File:') and summary revision IDs look mixed, though the vandalism itself is unmistakable.

value.what_changed_en: An anonymous editor reverted a previous editor's additions as 'block evasion' ('rv, eston kiertoa'), removing an unsourced interpretive paragraph arguing that the FCMA treaty technically obligated the Soviet Union to fight against its own potential attack, and restoring an earlier version with an inaccurate photo caption.
evidence: Toisin sanoen, sopimuksen sotilasosan nojalla Neuvostoliiton olisi tarvittaessa pitänyt avustaa Suomea tai jopa taistella myös omaa mahdollista hyökkäystään vastaan.
[[File:YYA-sopimus-1973.jpg|thumb|right|YYA-sopimusta allekirjoittamassa [[Finlandia-talo]]ssa vuonna 1973 presidentit [[Urho Kekkonen]] ja [[Nikolai Podgornyi]].]]
value.claim_en: Urho Kekkonen and Nikolai Podgornyi were both presidents signing the FCMA treaty at Finlandia Hall in 1973.
value.claim_fi: Presidentit Urho Kekkonen ja Nikolai Podgornyi olivat allekirjoittamassa YYA-sopimusta Finlandia-talossa vuonna 1973.
value.historical_note_en: The FCMA treaty was not signed in 1973 (a 1973 event in Finlandia Hall was the 25th-anniversary celebration, while extensions were signed in Moscow in 1970 and 1983), and Nikolai Podgornyi's title was Chairman of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet, not President.
value.uncertainty_note: This edit is itself a manual revert claiming block evasion ('rv, eston kiertoa') that was subsequently reverted back without an edit summary; it is unclear whether the anonymous editor was legitimately enforcing a block while accidentally restoring old errors, or engaging in an edit war / counter-reversion.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted an unsourced editorializing sentence stating that signing the Finno-Soviet Treaty of 1948 (YYA-sopimus) was a very big mistake by Finland. The edit was reverted after four minutes on neutrality grounds.
evidence: YYA-sopimuksen allekirjoittaminen oli Suomelta erittäin suuri virhe.
value.claim_en: Signing the Finno-Soviet Treaty of 1948 was a very big mistake by Finland.
value.claim_fi: YYA-sopimuksen allekirjoittaminen oli Suomelta erittäin suuri virhe.
value.narrative_en: Criticism of Finland's Cold War policy towards the Soviet Union

value.what_changed_en: Added unsourced evaluative commentary characterizing Urho Kekkonen's 1973 term extension by emergency law as occurring 'without elections' and being seen by some as 'the rock bottom of democratic deficit', while asserting that the president could dissolve parliament and the government 'almost arbitrarily'.
evidence: Nykyään jotkut pitävät kyseistä valintaa demokratiavajeen aallonpohjana.
hän saattoi halutessaan hajottaa eduskunnan ja hallituksen lähes mielivaltaisesti
value.claim_en: Urho Kekkonen's 1973 re-election without a vote is considered by some to be the nadir of Finland's democratic deficit, and in the 1970s the president held enough power to dissolve parliament and the cabinet almost arbitrarily.
value.claim_fi: Urho Kekkosen valintaa ilman vaaleja vuonna 1973 pidetään joidenkin mielestä demokratiavajeen aallonpohjana, ja 1970-luvulla presidentti saattoi hajottaa eduskunnan ja hallituksen lähes mielivaltaisesti.
value.narrative_en: Criticism of Kekkonen's autocratic power and democratic deficit in 1970s Finland
value.uncertainty_note: Could also be viewed as a good_faith_error (adding unsourced weasel-worded commentary that reflects real historical debate in Finland without proper attribution), though the loaded phrasing ('lähes mielivaltaisesti', 'demokratiavajeen aallonpohjana') and the reverter's note ('epäneutraaliakin') point primarily to pov_push.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced the SVG logo in the organization infobox with an older JPG logo and added the caption "The society's old emblem" ("Seuran vanha tunnus"), citing block evasion on Wikimedia Commons by the uploader of the SVG file. Another editor subsequently reverted this removal.
evidence: rv, eston kiertoa (WPK - kuva ladannut Commonsiin estetty käyttäjä, kts. Special:CentralAuth/Sariyr)
value.uncertainty_note: The edit is an administrative/policy enforcement attempt (reverting a Commons file uploaded by an allegedly blocked sockpuppet) that was itself reverted, creating ambiguity between 'content_dispute' (over whether to use a valid logo despite uploader block evasion) and 'other' (procedural/maintenance dispute).

value.what_changed_en: Replaced sourced, quoted historiographical descriptions of Finnish anti-Russian sentiment as a cultural narrative with unquoted, literal assertions emphasizing historical Russian atrocities (murdering, looting, enslaving children, and aiming to occupy, subjugate, and destroy Finland). It also removed a citation, a citation-needed tag, and a 'See also' link to 'Racism in Finland'.
evidence: Suomalaisia, myös lapsia vietiin orjiksi Venäjälle ja kaupattavaksi siellä edelleen.
value.claim_en: Anti-Russian sentiment in Finland is a long-standing reaction to historical Russian atrocities, enslavement of Finns, and attempts to occupy, subjugate, and destroy Finland, rather than a form of racism or a constructed victimhood myth.
value.claim_fi: Suomen venäläisvastaisuus on pitkäaikainen reaktio Venäjän historiallisiin julmuuksiin, suomalaisten orjuuttamiseen sekä pyrkimyksiin miehittää, alistaa ja tuhota Suomi, eikä niinkään rasismin muoto tai rakennettu uhrimyytti.
value.narrative_en: Justifying Finnish anti-Russian sentiment through historical Russian atrocities
value.uncertainty_note: The edit also engages in source manipulation by removing quotation marks around a cited source's characterization of a national myth and removing a reference tag elsewhere in the section, while the reverter labeled it vandalism ('sotkemisena').

value.what_changed_en: Inserted an unsourced sentence claiming that "for some reason, the Finland–Soviet Union Society is still operating," which was quickly reverted with a request for a source.
evidence: Jostakin syystä Suomi-Neuvostoliitto-seura on edelleen toiminnassa.
value.claim_en: The Finland–Soviet Union Society continues to operate.
value.claim_fi: Suomi–Neuvostoliitto-Seura on edelleen toiminnassa.
value.historical_note_en: Following the dissolution of the Soviet Union, the original Finland–Soviet Union Society was succeeded by the Finland-Russia Society (Suomi-Venäjä-Seura) in 1992.
value.uncertainty_note: A small splinter or neo-Stalinist group later registered the old name 'Suomi–Neuvostoliitto-Seura' in Finland, so the anonymous editor might have been referring to that fringe group or confusing the original society with the Finland-Russia Society, alongside using unencyclopedic tone ('for some reason').

value.what_changed_en: Replaced the word 'ystävien' ('friends', in the phrase 'among friends') with the ungrammatical and nonsensical phrase 'maahanmuuttaja poikia' ('immigrant boys'), while claiming in the edit summary to have fixed an error ('korjasin virheen').

Replaced a famous quote by President Urho Kekkonen ("This was the worst speech I have ever given, [but] I didn't write it myself") with joke song lyrics ("Kekkonen skis and Kekkonen fishes / how does Kekkonen do rock'n'roll?").
evidence: Tämä oli huonoin puhe, minkä olen koskaan pitänyt

value.what_changed_en: Replaced "accept the proposal" ("hyväksyä ehdotus") in a quote from President Kekkonen with "destroy ES" ("tuhota es", a Finnish meme abbreviation for the Euro Shopper energy drink), introduced deliberate misspellings into the quote, and deleted the word "politbyroo" (Politburo).
evidence: piasaada kansa vastus siihe, jatketanko ystävälismielistä ulkopolitikkaa

value.what_changed_en: Inserted two unsourced sentences claiming that Western countries initially offered aid to Finland during the 1961 Note Crisis, but withdrew the offer when it was revealed that President Kekkonen had ordered the Soviet note himself, adding that secret Foreign Ministry documents would open in 2011.
evidence: Länsimaat tarjosivat aluksi Suomelle apua, mutta peruivat tarjouksensa, koska paljastui, että nootti oli Kekkosen tilaama.
rv, "Länsimaat tarjosivat aluksi Suomelle apua, mutta peruivat tarjouksensa, koska paljastui, että nootti oli Kekkosen tilaama" wut?
value.claim_en: Western countries initially offered Finland aid during the 1961 Note Crisis, but withdrew their offer after discovering that President Kekkonen had commissioned the Soviet diplomatic note himself.
value.claim_fi: Länsimaat tarjosivat Suomelle apua noottikriisissä, mutta peruivat tarjouksensa paljastuttua, että presidentti Kekkonen oli itse tilannut nootin.
value.narrative_en: Conspiracy theory that Kekkonen ordered the 1961 Soviet note
value.historical_note_en: While rumours persisted in Finland that Kekkonen arranged the 1961 Soviet note to secure his re-election, archival research has found no evidence that Kekkonen ordered the note or that Western powers offered and then retracted aid over such a revelation.
value.uncertainty_note: It also pushes an anti-Kekkonen narrative (pov_push) and could be a good-faith repetition of a popular political rumour without citations, though stating an unproven rumour and an unsubstantiated claim about Western aid as established fact fits false_factual_claim best.

value.what_changed_en: Added claims attributed to Paavo Väyrynen stating that the Centre Party is controlled by Laestadians allied with the far right, along with trivial daily news snippets about Sipilä's speeches and poorly formatted citations. In the edit summary, the editor directly attacked Sipilä, asking why he deceives and oppresses the people and saying 'your master is from Pajala' (referring to Lars Levi Laestadius).
evidence: Miksi sinä Juha täällä kusetat odotuksilla ja kyykytät kansaa? Sinun herrasi on Pajalasta.
puoluetta hallitsevat äärioikeiston kanssa liittoutuneet saarnamies Lars Levi Laestadiuksen kannattajat.
Väyrynen, Paavo: puheenvuoroja eri tilaisuuksissa vuosina 2015-2016.
value.claim_en: Paavo Väyrynen has stated that Juha Sipilä's Centre Party is controlled by followers of preacher Lars Levi Laestadius who are allied with the far right.
value.claim_fi: Paavo Väyrynen on kertonut, että Juha Sipilän johtamaa keskustapuoluetta hallitsevat äärioikeiston kanssa liittoutuneet Lars Levi Laestadiuksen kannattajat.
value.narrative_en: Anti-Sipilä and anti-Laestadian political criticism
value.uncertainty_note: Whether Paavo Väyrynen actually made the exact 'far-right allied Laestadians' claim in his book is unverified here (which could also make this false_factual_claim or source_manipulation given the vague citations), though the hostile edit summary makes the editor's personal POV-pushing intent unmistakable.

value.what_changed_en: Rewrote the lead section to define the Finland–Soviet Union Society merely as the former name of the Finland–Russia Society from 1944 to 1991, adjusted formatting, and claimed the current name was adopted in 1991. It was reverted as block evasion by a long-term abuser ('WPK').
value.claim_en: The Finland–Soviet Union Society was the name of the Finland–Russia Society until 1991, and the name Finland–Russia Society was adopted in 1991.
value.claim_fi: Suomi–Neuvostoliitto-Seura oli Suomi–Venäjä-Seuran nimi vuoteen 1991, ja nykyinen nimi Suomi–Venäjä-Seura otettiin käyttöön vuonna 1991.
value.historical_note_en: The name was first changed to Suomen ja Venäjän kansojen ystävyysseura in December 1991, and the current name Suomi–Venäjä-Seura was actually adopted in 1992.
value.uncertainty_note: The edit combines a stylistic/structural rewrite typical of the banned sockpuppeteer 'WPK' (reverting purely for block evasion) with a minor date error (1991 vs. 1992 for the final name change), making 'other', 'false_factual_claim', and 'content_dispute' all plausible.

value.what_changed_en: Added a sourced sentence to the article's lead stating that according to a December 2022 Helsingin Sanomat Monthly Supplement article by Unto Hämäläinen, the Zavidovo leaker was presidential chief of staff Antero Jyränki, who used MP Erkki Tuomioja as a courier to pass the memo to journalist Tor Högnäs. The reverter undid the edit, commenting that this detail was not necessarily needed in the lead section.
evidence: Helsingin Sanomien kuukausiliitteen 12/2022 mukaan vuotaja oli tasavallan presidentin kansliapäällikkö [[Antero Jyränki]], joka käytti kansanedustaja [[Erkki Tuomioja|Erkki Tuomiojaa]] kuriirinaan toimittaessaan aineiston toimittaja [[Tor Högnäs|Tor Högnäsille]].
value.claim_en: According to a December 2022 investigative report by Unto Hämäläinen in Helsingin Sanomat, the Zavidovo memo was leaked by presidential chief of staff Antero Jyränki using MP Erkki Tuomioja as a courier to deliver it to journalist Tor Högnäs.
value.claim_fi: Unto Hämäläisen Helsingin Sanomien kuukausiliitteeseen joulukuussa 2022 kirjoittaman tutkivan jutun mukaan Zavidovo-muistion vuoti tasavallan presidentin kansliapäällikkö Antero Jyränki käyttäen kansanedustaja Erkki Tuomiojaa kuriirina toimittaakseen sen toimittaja Tor Högnäsille.
value.uncertainty_note: The diff appears to combine or interact with an earlier edit by the same IP (the revert summary notes reverting 3 edits, and removed_text has fragments from a prior version). Could also be classified as good_faith_error (misplaced content in the lead), though 'tätä ei välttämättä tarvita johdannossa' reflects an editorial disagreement over prominence in the lead section.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted a joke sentence inside a link to Urho Kekkonen, claiming that Kekkonen and others went to a nearby hot dog stand to buy gourmet hot dogs, which supposedly greatly affected Finland's geopolitical position.
evidence: Tämän jälkeen Kekkonen ja muut menivät viereiselle nakki kioskille josta he ostivat gurmee nakkisämpylät tämä on vaikuttanut suuresti suomen asemaan koska Kekkonen tarjosi muille jäsenille nakkisämpylät.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted a mocking sentence into the 'External links' section saying 'In reality, everyone hated erkki [Erkki Tuomioja], because he was one of those men' (a Finnish euphemism implying homosexuality).
evidence: Oikeasti, kaikki vihasivat erkkiä, sillä hän oli niitä miehiä.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced multiple words and phrases throughout the article on the Night Frost Crisis with absurd jokes, such as changing 'made its dissatisfaction clear' to 'made a bomb attack', adding that Kekkonen 'crowned himself king', and replacing 'leash' ('liekanaru') with 'jump rope' ('hyppynaru').

Attempted to simplify piped wikilinks with the summary 'kh' (kielenhuolto, copyediting) and added a citation needed template ({{Lähde}}), but broke both links by creating ungrammatical Finnish inflections ('Maalaisliitton') and malformed bracket syntax ('Kommunistinen Puolue]e]').
Inserted an unsourced, mocking claim stating that members of the Finland–Russia Society greatly admire Russia and hope for Finland to join or be annexed by Russia.
evidence: Jäsenet arvostavat Venäjää suuresti ja toivovat Suomen liittymistä tai liittämistä Venäjään.
value.claim_en: Members of the Finland–Russia Society greatly admire Russia and hope for Finland to join or be annexed by Russia.
value.claim_fi: Suomi–Venäjä-Seuran jäsenet arvostavat Venäjää suuresti ja toivovat Suomen liittymistä tai liittämistä Venäjään.
value.narrative_en: Portraying the Finland–Russia Society as treasonous or seeking annexation by Russia
value.historical_note_en: The Finland–Russia Society is a civic organization dedicated to cultural and bilateral cooperation between Finland and Russia, not an irredentist movement advocating annexation.
value.uncertainty_note: Could also be classified as pov_push or false_factual_claim, as it functions as political mockery and defamation against the society rather than pure nonsense or profanity.

value.what_changed_en: Appended a clause to the opening sentence defining the Paasikivi–Kekkonen line as a policy in which Finland took into account the security interests of the Soviet Union.
evidence: , jossa Suomi otti huomioon Neuvostoliiton turvallisuusintressit.
value.claim_en: In the Paasikivi–Kekkonen foreign policy line, Finland took into account the security interests of the Soviet Union.
value.claim_fi: Paasikiven–Kekkosen linjassa Suomi otti huomioon Neuvostoliiton turvallisuusintressit.
value.uncertainty_note: The added clause is a standard historical characterization of the Paasikivi–Kekkonen line. Because it was reverted within 3 minutes with a generic rollback summary, it is unclear if the reverter considered the phrasing one-sided/Cold War rhetoric (pov_push), objected to an unsourced addition (good_faith_error), or reverted all edits from that IP address.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced the key facts of the Night Frost Crisis (Finland, the Soviet Union, 1958, and Nikita Khrushchev) with absurdly false names and dates (China, France, 1556, and the made-up name 'Hasuko Hiratsi').
value.claim_en: The Night Frost Crisis broke out between China and France in 1556 and was named by Hasuko Hiratsi.
value.claim_fi: Yöpakkaset oli Kiinan ja Ranskan suhteissa vuonna 1556 puhjennut kriisi, jolle antoi nimen Hasuko Hiratsi.
value.historical_note_en: The Night Frost Crisis (Yöpakkaset) was a diplomatic crisis between Finland and the Soviet Union in the autumn of 1958, named after a remark by Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev.

value.what_changed_en: Added a brief, unsourced sentence stating that the internet has been censored in Finland since 2007, linking to the article 'Internet censorship in Finland', with 'suomessa' left uncapitalised. The reverter removed it noting that it would require more detailed explanation.
evidence: Vuodesta 2007 alkaen suomessa [[Internet-sensuuri Suomessa|on sensuroitu internetiä]].
value.claim_en: The internet has been censored in Finland since 2007.
value.claim_fi: Suomessa on sensuroitu internetiä vuodesta 2007 alkaen.
value.narrative_en: Criticism of Finnish internet filtering as censorship
value.uncertainty_note: The edit likely refers to the 2007 Act on Preventive Measures against the Distribution of Child Pornography (voluntary ISP blocklist), which critics and the linked Wikipedia article commonly call 'internet censorship' while authorities view it as filtering illegal content; thus it sits on the border between a poorly contextualised good-faith addition (good_faith_error) and framing a contested topic one-sidedly as outright censorship (pov_push).

value.what_changed_en: Attempted to add banker Björn Wahlroos to the table of notable Taistoists (describing him as a youth activist and doctor of economics/bank director), while breaking the wikitext table syntax.
value.claim_en: Björn Wahlroos is a former youth activist of the Taistoist movement and a doctor of economics and bank director.
value.claim_fi: Björn Wahlroos on entinen taistolaisliikkeen nuorisoaktiivi sekä kauppatieteiden tohtori ja pankinjohtaja.
value.uncertainty_note: The revert summary restores the page past multiple edits by this IP; the removed text suggests the editor had already made a broken attempt to add Wahlroos immediately prior, and the edit was reverted primarily due to broken table formatting rather than factual inaccuracy (Wahlroos is famously a former Taistoist youth activist).

value.what_changed_en: Removed the logo from the infobox, altered the description of the society's historical continuity—claiming the 1940 Peace and Friendship Society should not be confused with the 1944 society and calling it a Soviet-led communist front organization—changed the year of the name change from 1995 to 1994, and made minor stylistic edits. The edit was reverted purely as block evasion ('eston kiertoa').
value.claim_en: The Finland–Russia Society was founded in 1944 as the Finland–Soviet Union Society, should not be confused with the 1940 Peace and Friendship Society (which was a Soviet-directed communist front organization), and adopted its current name in 1994.
value.claim_fi: Suomi–Venäjä-Seura on perustettu vuonna 1944 Suomi–Neuvostoliitto-Seurana, sitä ei pidä sekoittaa vuoden 1940 rauhan ja ystävyyden seuraan (joka oli Neuvostoliitosta johdettu kommunistinen peitejärjestö), ja se otti nykyisen nimensä käyttöön vuonna 1994.
value.narrative_en: Distancing the post-1944 Finland–Soviet Union Society from the radical 1940 Peace and Friendship Society
value.uncertainty_note: The revert was strictly procedural due to block evasion by a long-term banned user (WPK), rather than a direct rejection of all the edits. Furthermore, part of the edit changed a date from 1995 to 1994 while keeping the existing citation attached, which borders on source manipulation or a factual correction/error depending on what the source actually states, while the framing of historical continuity vs. separation leans toward a content dispute or POV.

value.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced, polemical sentence asserting that the political goal of the Taistoists was to abolish the prevailing democratic system and establish a Soviet-style dictatorship. The reverter removed it as an 'absurd throwaway remark'.
evidence: Poliittisenatavoitteena taistolaisilla oli luopua vallitsevasta demokraattisesta järjestelmästä ja pystyttää Neuvostoliiton kaltainen diktatuuri.
value.claim_en: The political goal of the Taistoists was to abandon the prevailing democratic system and establish a Soviet-style dictatorship.
value.claim_fi: Taistolaisten poliittisena tavoitteena oli luopua vallitsevasta demokraattisesta järjestelmästä ja pystyttää Neuvostoliiton kaltainen diktatuuri.
value.narrative_en: Anti-communist framing of Taistoism as explicitly anti-democratic dictatorship-seeking
value.uncertainty_note: While Taistoists strongly supported the Soviet system and the concept of the dictatorship of the proletariat, framing their explicit goal simply as 'abandoning democracy to set up a dictatorship' uses non-neutral, loaded terminology rather than encyclopedic description; could also border on content_dispute or good_faith_error depending on the editor's intent.

value.what_changed_en: The edit used find-and-replace to insert the vulgar Finnish insult "Runkkari" ("wanker") before almost every occurrence of the surname "Vanhanen" throughout the article (including breaking image filenames, URLs, and citation tags) and replaced "entinen poliitikko" ("former politician") with "runkkari".

Restored an older or alternative version of the article (claiming to revert block evasion), which added Swedish as an official language of the Finno-Soviet Treaty, added a photo caption claiming the treaty was signed in 1973, and replaced the mention of the Soviet Union starting the war by attacking Finland in 1939 with a passive reference to the war breaking out.
evidence: YYA-sopimusta allekirjoittamassa [[Finlandia-talo]]ssa vuonna 1973 presidentit [[Urho Kekkonen]] ja [[Nikolai Podgornyi]].

ennen kuin Neuvostoliitto aloitti
hyökkäämällä Suomeen 1939.
value.claim_en: The Finno-Soviet Treaty of 1948 had Swedish as one of its languages and was signed at Finlandia Hall in 1973.
value.claim_fi: YYA-sopimuksen yhtenä kielenä oli ruotsi ja sopimusta oltiin allekirjoittamassa Finlandia-talossa vuonna 1973.
value.historical_note_en: The 1948 Finno-Soviet Treaty (YYA-sopimus) was drawn up only in Finnish and Russian, its extensions were signed in 1955, 1970, and 1983 (1973 was the 25th anniversary celebration, not a signing), and the Winter War began with a Soviet invasion of Finland in November 1939.
value.uncertainty_note: The edit is a wholesale revert between two versions of the article ('rv, eston kiertoa' = 'rv, block evasion'), bundling factual errors, stylistic rewrites, and a softened phrasing of the 1939 Soviet attack; it could also be viewed as a content dispute or block-evasion revert war rather than a targeted factual claim.

value.what_changed_en: Removed Jyrki Katainen's infobox and replaced it with vulgar sexual insults and an accusation of treason (calling him a "traitor and someone who gives blowjobs to his father and has sex with Ville Siliämaa").
evidence: maanpetturi ja isältään suihinottaja joka harrastaa seksiä ville siliämaan kanssa
value.uncertainty_note: Note on data extraction: the edit timestamp is May 2013, whereas the removed_text snippet mentions June 2014 and Alexander Stubb as successor, suggesting the diff reconstruction or an accidental revert to an old vandalised revision may have mixed versions, though the inserted text is unambiguously vandalism.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced the existing article text about the Finnish social and healthcare reform from late 2013 with updated, duplicated text copied verbatim from the Ministry of Social Affairs and Health website regarding the March 2014 parliamentary agreement. It was reverted as a copyright violation and direct copy-paste.
evidence: Hallituspuolueet sopivat 23.3.2014 yhdessä oppositiopuolueiden kanssa sosiaali- ja terveyspalvelujen uudistuksesta.
value.claim_en: On March 23, 2014, Finnish government and opposition parties agreed to reorganize all social and healthcare services under five regional providers.
value.claim_fi: Hallituspuolueet sopivat 23.3.2014 yhdessä oppositiopuolueiden kanssa kaikkien sote-palvelujen järjestämisestä viiden vahvan alueellisen järjestäjän toimesta.

value.what_changed_en: The editor reverted recent text describing the March 2014 parliamentary agreement on five social and health care regions—citing that it was copied directly from the Ministry of Social Affairs and Health website (stm.fi)—and restored an older version describing an outdated December 2013 municipality-based proposal. The edit was later reverted with a summary stating that the Ministry itself had updated the page with accurate, up-to-date information.
evidence: STM päivittänyt oikeat, ajantasaiset tiedot sivulle
