value.what_changed_en: Added a paragraph to the criticism section claiming the Katainen Cabinet overrepresented Western Finland and had only one or two ministers from Eastern Finland out of 19, citing a Kymen Sanomat piece inline without proper formatting. The reverter removed it for pushing the editor's own interpretation (original research).
evidence: siellä on iso länsisuomalainen yliedustus ja hyvin vähän ministereitä Itä-Suomesta
Itä-Suomen edustus on aivan yhden tai kahden ministerin varassa 19:sta.
rv, tuossa kyllä näytettäisiin tunkevan omaa tulkintaa mukaan
value.claim_en: The Katainen Cabinet has been criticized for heavily overrepresenting Western Finland while having only one or two ministers out of 19 from Eastern Finland.
value.claim_fi: Kataisen hallituksen kokoonpanoa on kritisoitu länsisuomalaisesta yliedustuksesta ja siitä, että Itä-Suomen edustus on vain yhden tai kahden ministerin varassa 19:stä.
value.narrative_en: Regional underrepresentation of Eastern Finland in national politics
value.uncertainty_note: Without access to the cited Kymen Sanomat article (likely an opinion piece or letter to the editor), it is slightly ambiguous whether this is primarily an inexperienced editor's original research/synthesis ('good_faith_error') or mild regional 'pov_push'.

value.what_changed_en: Reverted premature changes that listed Katainen as Prime Minister back to Minister of Finance, and removed the sentence stating 'Katainen is becoming Prime Minister of Finland on June 23' with the summary 'let's wait calmly'.
evidence: Kataisesta on tulossa Suomen pääministeri 23. kesäkuuta.
value.claim_en: As of June 17, 2011, Jyrki Katainen is the Minister of Finance of Finland rather than the Prime Minister.
value.claim_fi: Jyrki Katainen on 17. kesäkuuta 2011 Suomen valtiovarainministeri eikä pääministeri.
value.uncertainty_note: The edit itself was an accurate maintenance revert of premature IP edits (Katainen formally took office on June 22, 2011); without a revert summary, it is unclear whether the subsequent revert restored the premature Prime Minister title or simply re-added the note about his upcoming appointment.

value.what_changed_en: Added subsections criticizing Jyrki Katainen's stance on mandatory Swedish ('Pakkoruotsi') and the sale of the state-owned company Destia, implying cronyism via Bilderberg Group connections. It also duplicated an existing section on campaign finance and added unreliable conspiracy blogs and forum links as sources.
evidence: Ahlström-sukuun kuuluva Krister Ahlström on osallistunut Kataiselle hyvin tuttuun Bilderberg-kokoukseen
rv, samat asiat kahteen kertaan, huonosti lähteistettyä ja merkitykseltään kyseenalaista
value.claim_en: Jyrki Katainen opposed removing mandatory Swedish instruction and sold the state-owned company Destia cheaply to Ahlström Capital, whose family member attended the Bilderberg meetings familiar to Katainen.
value.claim_fi: Jyrki Katainen vastusti pakkoruotsista luopumista ja myi valtionyhtiö Destian halvalla Ahlström Capitalille, jonka sukuun kuuluva henkilö on osallistunut Kataiselle tuttuun Bilderberg-kokoukseen.
value.narrative_en: Anti-establishment and Bilderberg conspiracy critique of Jyrki Katainen
value.historical_note_en: Destia's annual revenue in 2013 was approximately 400–450 million euros, not 1.2 billion euros as claimed in the inserted text.
value.uncertainty_note: The edit combines POV-pushing with false factual claims (inflated revenue figure), unreliable conspiracy sources (source manipulation), and accidental duplication of an existing section.

value.what_changed_en: Added a subsection under 'Campaigns' for the National Whisky Party ('Kansallinen Viskipuolue'), including its campaign slogan ('Against unnecessary regulation and paternalism. For reason and freedom') and a reference to its website. It was reverted through a brief edit war as non-notable ('Epämerkittävä'), likely because it was not a registered political party at the time.
evidence: * '''Vaalilause:''' Turhaa sääntelyä ja holhousta vastaan. Järjen ja vapauden puolesta.
value.claim_en: The National Whisky Party is campaigning in the 2015 Finnish parliamentary election with the slogan 'Against unnecessary regulation and paternalism. For reason and freedom.'
value.claim_fi: Kansallinen Viskipuolue kampanjoi vuoden 2015 eduskuntavaaleissa vaalilauseella 'Turhaa sääntelyä ja holhousta vastaan. Järjen ja vapauden puolesta.'
value.uncertainty_note: The edit summary bundles multiple edits and reverts together. Depending on the editor's intent, adding an unregistered minor political association could also be seen as a good-faith error regarding Wikipedia's inclusion criteria or promotional editing ('other' / 'pov_push').

value.what_changed_en: Inserted two repetitive paragraphs claiming that former Prime Minister Mari Kiviniemi was evicted from the official residence Kesäranta on 22 June 2011 and had to be forcibly carried out by police while clinging to a dining room chair.
evidence: pitäen kynsin hampain ruokasalin tuolista kiinni
poliisi joutui kantamaan hänet väkivalloin ulos sieltä
value.claim_en: Mari Kiviniemi was evicted from Kesäranta on 22 June 2011 and had to be forcibly carried out by the police after clinging to a dining room chair.
value.claim_fi: Mari Kiviniemi häädettiin Kesärannasta 22. kesäkuuta 2011 ja poliisi joutui kantamaan hänet väkivalloin ulos hänen pidettyään kiinni ruokasalin tuolista.
value.historical_note_en: Mari Kiviniemi handed over the Prime Minister's office and residence peacefully to Jyrki Katainen on 22 June 2011 without any eviction or police intervention.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced three-letter electoral district abbreviations (e.g., HEL, UUS) in a results table header with the full names of the districts (e.g., Helsingin, Uudenmaan) and added two subsection headings ('Results nationwide' and 'Results by electoral district'). It was reverted because the full names were already accessible via the hyperlinks and likely made the table too wide.
evidence: Vaalipiirin koko nimen näkee tarvittassa hyperlinkistä.
value.uncertainty_note: Could also be viewed as a minor formatting content_dispute, as both ways of labelling the table headers are valid editorial choices.

value.what_changed_en: Added a duplicated list of 2017 policy demands by the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation and claimed that the Sipilä cabinet froze wind power subsidies in 2016 to investigate the risk of exploding bats, citing news articles that actually attributed the bat claim to the Finns Party rather than the whole government. The reverter removed it as off-topic advocacy and trivial detail.
evidence: [[Suomen luonnonsuojeluliitto]] vaati syksyllä 2017 ympäristölle haitallisten tukien karsintaa ja tukea metsiensuojeluun.
Sipilän hallitus jäädytti tuulivoimatuet vuonna 2016, koska se halusi selvittää riskin lepakoiden räjähtelyyn tuulivoimasta.
Perussuomalaiset haluaa keskeyttää tuulivoimaloiden rakentamisen ”räjähtelevien lepakoiden” takia
aihe edelleen hallitus, ei SLL. lepakoiden räjähtely kokonaisuuden kannalta nippelitietoa
value.claim_en: The Finnish Association for Nature Conservation demanded cuts to environmentally harmful subsidies in autumn 2017, and the Sipilä cabinet froze wind power subsidies in 2016 to investigate the risk of bats exploding due to wind turbines.
value.claim_fi: Suomen luonnonsuojeluliitto vaati syksyllä 2017 ympäristölle haitallisten tukien karsintaa, ja Sipilän hallitus jäädytti tuulivoimatuet vuonna 2016 selvittääkseen riskin lepakoiden räjähtelystä tuulivoiman vuoksi.
value.narrative_en: Environmentalist critique and ridicule of the Sipilä cabinet's energy and environmental policies
value.uncertainty_note: Also contains elements of false_factual_claim / source_manipulation (attributing a Finns Party parliamentary group statement about 'exploding bats' to the entire cabinet freezing subsidies) and content_dispute over due weight and relevance.

value.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced section about 'Hetemäki's working group and other background influencers' (including the Confederation of Finnish Industries, EK, and the National Coalition Party's core group) as well as a subsection highlighting Jyrki Katainen's and Finnish business leaders' attendance at Bilderberg meetings. The reverter removed it for lacking sources.
evidence: Myös Kokoomuksen ydinryhmä ja EK vaikuttivat.
Katainen itse osallistui myös Bilderberg-kokouseen, kuten Jorma Ollila , [[Henrik Ehrnrooth|Henrik Ehrenrooth]] ja [[Krister Ahlström]].
value.claim_en: The Katainen cabinet was substantially influenced behind the scenes by Martti Hetemäki's working group, the Confederation of Finnish Industries (EK), the National Coalition Party's inner circle, and connections to the Bilderberg meetings.
value.claim_fi: Kataisen hallituksen toimintaan vaikuttivat merkittävästi taustalla Martti Hetemäen työryhmä, Elinkeinoelämän keskusliitto, Kokoomuksen ydinryhmä sekä yhteydet Bilderberg-kokouksiin.
value.narrative_en: Elite and corporate behind-the-scenes control of government policy
value.uncertainty_note: While the individual facts (the existence of Hetemäki's economic working group and Katainen's Bilderberg attendance) are real, grouping them unsourced under 'background influencers' frames the cabinet through an elite/conspiratorial lens; however, it could also be seen as a good_faith_error by an editor adding unsourced political commentary.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted an unsourced paragraph into the 'Childhood and youth' section alleging that media coverage of Matti Vanhanen's father Tatu Vanhanen arriving shoeless to an interview and the National Bureau of Investigation dropping an investigation into his 'far-right racial theory writings' smoothed Matti Vanhanen's path as prime minister, and claiming Tatu Vanhanen's influence is visible in Matti Vanhanen's labor reform.
evidence: Keskusrikospoliisi otti tutkittavaksi ja samalla lopetti Tatu Vanhasen äärioikeistolaista rotuoppikirjoittelua koskevan rikostutkinnan.
Isä Tatun kengättömyys ja tutkimatta jättäminen silottivat Anneli Jäätteenmäen tilalle nostetun Matti Vanhasen tien pääministerinä.
Tatu Vanhasen vaikutus Matti Vanhasen ajatteluun näkyy muun muassa Matti Vanhasen muotoilemassa työreformissa.
value.claim_en: Dropping a criminal investigation into Tatu Vanhanen's racial writings smoothed Matti Vanhanen's path as prime minister, and Tatu Vanhanen's thinking influenced Matti Vanhanen's labor reform.
value.claim_fi: Tatu Vanhasen rotukirjoittelua koskevan rikostutkinnan lopettaminen silotti Matti Vanhasen tietä pääministerinä, ja isän ajattelu vaikutti Matti Vanhasen muotoilemaan työreformiin.
value.narrative_en: Discrediting Matti Vanhanen by associating his policies and career with his father's controversial race and IQ theories
value.historical_note_en: The 2004 Helsingin Sanomat Kuukausiliite interview that prompted the NBI to consider and decline a preliminary investigation into Tatu Vanhanen's statements on race and IQ took place more than a year after Matti Vanhanen became Prime Minister in June 2003.
value.uncertainty_note: The diff appears to build on an immediately preceding edit by the same editor (the revert summary notes reverting the last 2 edits, and 'tutkittavaksi' was already present in removed_text), and mixes speculative political commentary with chronological/factual inaccuracies.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced the full names of Finnish electoral districts (e.g., 'Helsingin', 'Uudenmaan') in a results table with three-letter abbreviations (e.g., 'HEL', 'UUS') and removed two subheadings ('Result in the whole country' and 'Result by electoral district'). Both the edit and its revert were accompanied by summaries debating table layout and clarity.
evidence: Vaalipiirin koko nimen näkee tarvittassa hyperlinkistä.
Tuo koko nimi nyt ei todellakaan pidennä taulukkoa, joten selvyyden vuoksi näin.

value.what_changed_en: Re-added a sourced section titled 'Strip-search controversy' ('Ruumiintarkastuskohu') describing Suvi Lindén's February 2009 statement that companies can force employees to undergo strip searches under existing law, along with a law professor's rebuttal. The reverting editor removed it as recentism not suitable for an encyclopedia unless it had lasting career impact.
evidence: Helmikuussa 2009 Suvi Lindén ilmaisi [[Lex Nokia]]an liittyvänä mielipiteenään, että yritykset voivat jo nykyisen lainsäädännön mukaan tarvittaessa pakottaa työntekijänsä ruumiintarkastukseen.
value.claim_en: In February 2009, Suvi Lindén mistakenly claimed during the Lex Nokia debate that employers can legally force employees to undergo strip searches, which a labour law professor refuted.
value.claim_fi: Helmikuussa 2009 Suvi Lindén väitti Lex Nokia -keskustelun yhteydessä virheellisesti työnantajien voivan pakottaa työntekijöitään ruumiintarkastukseen, minkä työoikeuden professori kumosi.
value.uncertainty_note: Adding negative daily news about a politician can also carry an element of POV-pushing (undue weight to embarrass the subject), though the text itself is neutrally worded and sourced.

value.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced section titled "KMS" describing an alleged car conversation between businessman Arto Merisalo and Mari Kiviniemi regarding campaign financing, along with Kiviniemi's denial. The reverter removed it as an unnecessary and unsourced detail.
evidence: Liikemies Arto Merisalo kertoi keskustelleensa autossaan Mari Kiviniemen kanssa vaalirahoituksesta ajomatkalla Toivo Sukarin omistamasta Lemäpäälän Ideparkista Tampereelle.
value.claim_en: Businessman Arto Merisalo stated that he discussed campaign financing with Mari Kiviniemi during a car ride from Lempäälä's Ideapark to Tampere, which Kiviniemi denied.
value.claim_fi: Liikemies Arto Merisalo kertoi keskustelleensa Mari Kiviniemen kanssa vaalirahoituksesta automatkalla Lempäälän Ideaparkista Tampereelle, minkä Kiviniemi kiisti.
value.narrative_en: 2007 Finnish campaign finance scandal (KMS)
value.uncertainty_note: Could also be viewed as a content_dispute over encyclopedic relevance (undue weight) or mild pov_push to highlight a political scandal, though the phrasing includes Kiviniemi's denial and the revert primarily cited the lack of sources and triviality.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted an unsourced policy suggestion arguing that healthcare could apply regulations similar to private schools, and edited an existing sentence (likely added in an immediately preceding edit by the same IP) to state that funding is restricted to per-pupil grants rather than merely funded by them. The reverter rolled back two consecutive edits as opinion ('mielipide').
evidence: Lisäksi terveydenhuoltoon voisi voisi soveltaa samanlaisia säädöksiä kuin [[Yksityiskoulu|yksityisiin kouluihin]]
value.claim_en: Healthcare could apply regulations similar to those for private schools, limiting operational funding to state and municipal per-capita grants.
value.claim_fi: Terveydenhuoltoon voisi soveltaa samanlaisia säädöksiä kuin yksityisiin kouluihin, jolloin toiminnan rahoitus rajataan valtiolta ja kunnilta saataviin avustuksiin.
value.narrative_en: Advocating a private-school funding model for Finnish healthcare reform
value.uncertainty_note: Because this is the second of two consecutive edits reverted together, part of the modified text comes from the IP's own immediately preceding edit; it could also be classified as a good_faith_error (original research/editorialising by an inexperienced user unaware of Wikipedia's neutrality rules).

value.what_changed_en: Re-inserted a sourced bullet point quoting columnist Taina West saying that although Timo Soini labeled the major parties old and tired, the Finns Party ('persut') is 'no youth movement either'. The editor placed this comment inside a list of tax reform working group recommendations, and it was reverted as an unnecessary detail in the wrong section.
evidence: Soini on leimannut suuret puolueet vanhoiksi ja väsyneiksi, mutta [[Taina West]]in mukaan eivät "persutkaan mikään nuorisoliike ole".
Älä poista lähteistettyä tekstiä, jos piakka ei miellytä siirrä sopivaan.
Oli kohdassa Verotuksen kehittämistyöryhmän suositukset | Tarpeeton yksittäinen yksityiskohta, ei kuulu artikkeliin, ei tuohon kohtaan eikä tuossa muodossa.
value.claim_en: Although Timo Soini has labeled the major parties as old and tired, columnist Taina West argues that the Finns Party is not a youth movement either.
value.claim_fi: Vaikka Timo Soini on leimannut suuret puolueet vanhoiksi ja väsyneiksi, kolumnisti Taina Westin mukaan perussuomalaisetkaan ei ole mikään nuorisoliike.
value.narrative_en: Criticism of the Finns Party during the 2011 election
value.uncertainty_note: Borders on content_dispute and good_faith_error (due to the misplaced section), as editors disagreed on the encyclopedic relevance of a single election-day newspaper column, though insisting on inserting a pointed jab at a party on election day leans toward mild POV pushing.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced the claim that 20 ministers is the largest number in Finnish history with a statement that the cabinet has two more ministers than the previous Vanhanen cabinet, referring to the talk page.
evidence: nykyhallituksessa siis kaksi enemmän kuin edellisessä Vanhasen hallituksessa
value.claim_en: Vanhanen's second cabinet has two more ministers than the previous Vanhanen cabinet, rather than 20 ministers being the largest number in Finnish history.
value.claim_fi: Vanhasen toisessa hallituksessa on kaksi ministeriä enemmän kuin edellisessä Vanhasen hallituksessa, eikä 20 ministeriä ole suurin määrä Suomen historiassa.
value.uncertainty_note: Without seeing the talk page discussion ('keskustelusivu'), it is unclear whether the debate was over historical definitions of ministers/senators (e.g. counting cabinets with changes vs. initial size) or whether one editor made a good-faith factual error.

value.what_changed_en: Added a new section titled 'Ongelmia ulkoistamisessa' ('Problems in outsourcing') listing selected local controversies and news stories about private healthcare companies (Pihlajalinna, Attendo, Mehiläinen) with raw URLs. The edit was reverted with the summary 'ei sovi tähän artikkeliin' ('does not belong in this article'), as the anecdotes were off-topic for an article about the national regional government and health/social services reform.
evidence: SOTE-palvelujen ulkoistaminen on tuottanut tukun ongelmia. Esimerkiksi:
value.claim_en: Outsourcing health and social services in Finland has caused numerous problems in private care facilities and procurement processes.
value.claim_fi: Sosiaali- ja terveyspalvelujen ulkoistaminen on aiheuttanut lukuisia ongelmia yksityisissä hoivakodeissa ja hankinnoissa.
value.narrative_en: Opposition to privatization and outsourcing of public healthcare and social services
value.uncertainty_note: The edit also exhibits traits of a good_faith_error (misplaced content and unformatted inline URLs), as reflected in the reverter's summary about article scope, though the selective compilation of negative news stories under 'a bunch of problems' clearly pushes an anti-outsourcing angle.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted internet memes and forum trolling across multiple edits, including claims that the pandemic sparked discussion about Ylilauta administrator Sopsy's sexual orientation and Bora's mental health issues, an atheist meme quote ("Euphoria or godlessness is an emotional state that can be achieved by becoming enlightened by one's own intelligence"), and nonsensical typos like "2020pl", interspersed with legitimate updates.
evidence: Koronaviruspandemia on aiheuttanut Suomessa keskustelua muun muassa Sopsyn seksuaalisesta suuntautumisesta sekä Boran mielenterveyden ongelmista.
Euforia eli jumalattomuus on tunnetila, jonka voi saavuttaa valaistumalla omasta älykkyydestään.
value.uncertainty_note: The record aggregates multiple edits and reverts over several days (referencing May 12–24, 2020), combining genuine statistical updates and reverts by regular editors with block-evading trolling from a known forum vandal (WPK / Ylilauta).

value.what_changed_en: Replaced the article's lead section on the COVID-19 pandemic in Finland with a long satirical parody text (likely copied from Hikipedia/Uncyclopedia) about 'wrong opinions', Activia yogurt, Pastafarianism, and politician Jussi Halla-aho.
evidence: '''Väärät mielipiteet''' eli ennakkoluulot ovat joukko mielipiteitä, joita vastaan ei tarvitse minkäänlaisia perusteluja, koska on jo niin itsestäänselvää että ne ovat kakkaa.

value.what_changed_en: While attempting to undo a previous edit by the same anonymous user, the edit corrupted citation tags and templates throughout the text with URL-encoded HTML entities and left broken wikilink syntax (`[[`). Because both removed and inserted blocks are truncated, it is also possible that an entire passage in the 'Youth politician' section was removed in an earlier edit and partially restored here with mangled markup.
value.uncertainty_note: Both removed_text and inserted_text are truncated with '…', making it unclear whether the editor was purely self-reverting a broken browser/proxy edit (resulting in URL-encoded markup corruption) or also removing/restoring substantive text around the 'kavkaz.fi' Baltic Star reference.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced the upcoming-event template at the top of the article with mocking graffiti claiming that Wikipedia user Vyörykkä will vote for Satan in these municipal elections, while breaking the opening bracket of the election infobox template.

Added unsourced critical details and quotes about the Finnish 'active model' for unemployment benefits, including MP Juhana Vartiainen's party affiliation and his statement that making unemployed life more strenuous is good, changed a phrasing from 'did not cut' to 'cut about every second benefit recipient's', and inserted an unattributed quote calling the model's passage 'my biggest mistake'.
evidence: on hyvä, että aktiivimalli tekee työttömän elämästä rasittavampaa. Mallin
"Suurin virheeni oli, että laskin aktiivimallin tuollaisenaan läpi. Siihen jäi se valuvika, että ihminen saa sanktion, vaikka tekee kaikkensa hakeakseen töitä", hän toteaa.
value.claim_en: Proponents of the active model stated it was good to make unemployed people's lives more strenuous, the model cut benefits for about half of recipients, and a responsible politician later admitted passing it as-is was their biggest mistake.
value.claim_fi: Aktiivimallin puolustajan mukaan oli hyvä tehdä työttömän elämästä rasittavampaa, malli leikkasi noin joka toisen tuensaajan etuutta ja siitä vastannut poliitikko piti sen läpipäästämistä suurimpana virheenään.
value.narrative_en: Criticism of the Sipilä government's unemployment 'active model' (aktiivimalli)
value.uncertainty_note: The added quotes (by Juhana Vartiainen and likely Juha Sipilä or Jari Lindström) correspond to real media statements from 2018–2019, and the revert rolled back 4 consecutive edits at once; without seeing the surrounding sentences for each diff hunk or the other 3 edits, this could also be seen as an unsourced content dispute or good-faith addition rather than one-sided POV pushing.

value.what_changed_en: Added two poorly formatted subsections with news citations about September 2020 COVID-19 measures (mask recommendations, hospital visits, and travel restrictions), containing numerous typos, sentence fragments, out-of-order dates, and content that the reverter noted did not match the cited sources.
evidence: lisätty sisältö ei vastaa tietolähdettä eikä ajankohdat täsmää
value.claim_en: In September 2020, the Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL) tightened hospital visitation guidelines, considered stricter mask recommendations for schools and shopping centers, and Finland planned to reimpose travel restrictions on countries such as Estonia and Sweden.
value.claim_fi: Syyskuussa 2020 Terveyden ja hyvinvoinnin laitos (THL) tiukensi sairaalavierailujen ohjeistusta ja harkitsi tiukempaa maskisuositusta kouluihin ja kauppakeskuksiin, minkä lisäksi Suomen oli määrä asettaa muun muassa Viro ja Ruotsi uudelleen matkustusrajoitusten piiriin.
value.uncertainty_note: Because the reverter noted that the added text did not match the cited sources and dates were wrong, this borders on source_manipulation or false_factual_claim, though the heavy typos and garbled sentences strongly point to an incompetent good-faith attempt to update current events.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted the derogatory nickname 'Huulipunahallitus' ('Lipstick Government') twice into the article, claiming in the edit summary to have corrected the government's real name.
value.claim_en: The Marin Cabinet is also known as the 'Lipstick Government'.
value.claim_fi: Marinin hallitus tunnetaan myös nimellä Huulipunahallitus.
value.narrative_en: Sexist mockery of the female-led Marin Cabinet
value.uncertainty_note: Although 'huulipunahallitus' was an actual pejorative term used in public discourse against the female-led coalition, inserting it unsourced into the lead with the sarcastic summary 'corrected the real name of the government' makes it deliberate mockery/vandalism rather than a neutral or merely POV-pushing addition.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced the sourced statement that Finland's unemployment 'activation model' was copied from Denmark with an unsourced claim that it was merely marketed using the Danish model, which differed greatly from what was implemented in Finland. Because the existing citation to Helsingin Sanomat remained attached to the sentence, the edit also altered the text in front of a source without updating the citation.
evidence: Suomen aktiivimallia markkinoitiin Tanskan mallilla, joka poikkeaa suuresti Suomessa toteutuneesta
value.claim_en: Finland's unemployment activation model was marketed using the Danish model, which differs greatly from the model actually implemented in Finland.
value.claim_fi: Suomen aktiivimallia markkinoitiin Tanskan mallilla, joka poikkeaa suuresti Suomessa toteutuneesta mallista.
value.narrative_en: Criticism of the Sipilä government's unemployment activation model
value.uncertainty_note: In Finnish public debate, experts and critics did point out major differences between the Danish flexicurity system and the Finnish activation model, so this could also be seen as a good_faith_error (adding unsourced commentary over an existing citation) or source_manipulation (changing a cited sentence so it no longer matches the source).

value.what_changed_en: Added an empty, unsourced subsection heading stating 'December 28 restriction of the COVID pass for three weeks', without any body text or references. It was reverted as unsourced and unclear.
value.claim_en: The Finnish COVID-19 pass was restricted for three weeks starting on December 28, 2021.
value.claim_fi: Suomen koronapassia rajoitettiin kolmeksi viikoksi 28. joulukuuta 2021 alkaen.

value.what_changed_en: Added unsourced entries about 2020s Finnish culture, sports, and deaths—including singer Tapani Kansa's death in 2025, the 2024 film Stormskerry Maja, several sports achievements (floorball, Saga Vanninen, U16 women's basketball, Davis Cup, futsal), an image of Nokia Arena, and a new subsection on the 2025 transition to HD television—and changed a description from 'muusikko' (musician) to 'iskelmälaulaja' (schlager singer).
value.claim_en: Notable events in Finland in the 2020s include the 2025 death of Tapani Kansa, the 2024 film Stormskerry Maja, major international achievements in floorball, athletics, youth basketball, tennis, and futsal, the completion of Nokia Arena, and the 2025 phase-out of standard-definition television broadcasts.
value.claim_fi: Suomen 2020-luvun merkittäviin tapahtumiin kuuluvat Tapani Kansan kuolema vuonna 2025, vuoden 2024 elokuva Myrskyluodon Maija, suuret kansainväliset saavutukset salibandyssa, yleisurheilussa, nuorten koripallossa, tenniksessä ja futsalissa, Nokia-areenan valmistuminen sekä SD-televisiolähetysten päättyminen vuonna 2025.

value.what_changed_en: Updated daily COVID-19 statistics, variant case numbers, dates, and citation access date from February 16 to February 17, 2021. The edit was reverted because the date associated with the updated variant case figures was inaccurate.
evidence: päivitys ei hyväksyttävä, muutovirustartuntojen pvm väärä
value.claim_en: By February 17, 2021, Finland had 51,595 confirmed COVID-19 cases (including 548 new cases) and 427 variant cases.
value.claim_fi: 17. helmikuuta 2021 mennessä Suomessa oli 51 595 vahvistettua koronavirustartuntaa, joista 548 uusia, sekä 427 muuntovirustartuntaa.

value.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced sentence stating that former Centre Party chair Katri Kulmuni also expressed having wanted the party to go into opposition after its election defeat, but said she remained in the minority as others supported joining the government. The edit was reverted for lacking a citation ('lähteetön').
evidence: Myös Keskustan entinen puheenjohtaja [[Katri Kulmuni]] on ilmaissut itse halunneensa vaalitappion jälkeen Keskustan olevan oppositiossa, mutta kertonut jääneensä vähemmistöön muiden kannattaessa hallituksessa mukana oloa.
value.claim_en: Former Centre Party chair Katri Kulmuni stated that she personally wanted the party to enter the opposition after its election loss, but remained in the minority as others favoured participating in the government.
value.claim_fi: Keskustan entinen puheenjohtaja Katri Kulmuni on kertonut halunneensa puolueen jäävän oppositioon vaalitappion jälkeen, mutta jääneensä asiassa vähemmistöön.

value.what_changed_en: Updated the COVID-19 case, death, incidence, and recovery statistics in a table for hospital districts in Finland, removed a reference, and introduced several unclosed bold formatting tags. The edit was reverted because the updated estimate of 2,500 recovered patients was not found in the cited source.
evidence: lukua parantuneet arviolta 2 500 ei ole tietolähteessä, viitattava paremmin
value.claim_en: As of 26 April 2020, Finland had 4,576 confirmed COVID-19 cases, 190 deaths, and approximately 2,500 recovered patients.
value.claim_fi: 26. huhtikuuta 2020 Suomessa oli 4 576 vahvistettua koronavirustartuntaa, 190 kuollutta ja arviolta 2 500 parantunutta.
value.uncertainty_note: The revert rolled back two edits by two different IP addresses simultaneously; while this edit updated the recovery figure to ~2,500 without updating its source (whichcould lean towards source_manipulation), it is clearly a sincere statistical update lacking proper citation rather than deliberate misrepresentation.

value.what_changed_en: Updated the COVID-19 case and death statistics in Finland from October 20 to October 21, 2020 (e.g., changing cases from 13,849 to 14,071 and adding "4 new coronavirus deaths"), while removing the existing citations without providing new sources and introducing minor formatting/spelling errors.
value.claim_en: By October 21, 2020, Finland had 14,071 confirmed COVID-19 cases (222 new) and 355 deaths (4 new), with incidence rising.
value.claim_fi: 21. lokakuuta 2020 mennessä Suomessa oli 14 071 vahvistettua koronavirustartuntaa (222 uutta) ja 355 kuolemaa (4 uutta), ja ilmaantuvuus oli nousussa.
value.uncertainty_note: The edit also removed citations while updating the numbers, which touches on source_manipulation, though the intent clearly appears to be an unsourced good-faith attempt to update daily pandemic statistics (13,849 + 222 = 14,071; 351 + 4 = 355).

value.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced sentence to the 'Interpretations' section stating that the strong non-socialist (bourgeois) parliamentary majority (113–87) formed in the 1962 elections was regarded as a reminder to the Soviet Union about the limits of acceptable interference in Finland's internal affairs.
evidence: Toisaalta eduskuntaan muodostunutta vankkaa porvarienemmistöä (113−87) pidettiin muistutuksena Neuvostoliitolle siitä, missä määrin sen oli sopivaa puuttua Suomen sisäisiin asioihin.
value.claim_en: The strong bourgeois parliamentary majority of 113–87 formed in the 1962 Finnish parliamentary election was regarded as a reminder to the Soviet Union of the limits to interfering in Finland's internal affairs.
value.claim_fi: Eduskuntaan muodostunutta vankkaa porvarienemmistöä (113–87) pidettiin muistutuksena Neuvostoliitolle siitä, missä määrin sen oli sopivaa puuttua Suomen sisäisiin asioihin.
value.uncertainty_note: Because the revert summary uses a standard rollback message without explanation, it is unclear whether the edit was reverted strictly for lacking a citation and using passive weasel words ('pidettiin' / 'was regarded'), as original research, or as subtle ideological framing (pov_push) downplaying Kekkonen's consolidation of power.

value.what_changed_en: Added several custom-parameterized URLs to a generic online COVID-19 simulator ('Epidemic Calculator') in the 'External links' section, presenting the editor's own hypothetical simulation runs (e.g., for Uusimaa and a city the size of Lahti) as estimates of the epidemic in Finland. The reverter removed them as original research/trivia using a non-Finland-specific tool.
evidence: Neljäs arvio. Lahden kokoinen kaupunki noin 113000 as, alussa vain yksi tautitapaus.

Eri parametreilla tällä yksittäisellä simulaatiolla saadut tulokset ovat triviaa ja korkeintaan yksi esimerkki saa riittää. Simulaatio ei myöskään ole mitenkään erikoistunut kuvamaan epidemian leviämistä Suomessa
value.claim_en: Custom parameterizations of the generic online Epidemic Calculator provide specific mortality and spread estimates for the COVID-19 epidemic in Finland, Uusimaa, and a city the size of Lahti.
value.claim_fi: Yleiskäyttöisen Epidemic Calculator -verkkolaskimen eri parametrisoinnit tarjoavat arvioita koronaepidemian kehityksestä ja kuolleisuudesta Suomessa, Uudellamaalla ja Lahden kokoisessa kaupungissa.

value.what_changed_en: Across a bundled sequence of anonymous edits, editors replaced parts of the lead paragraph with vulgar graffiti (e.g. 'hannele sits on my face', 'naughty', 'freaky elsa'), changed Kekkonen's middle name from Kaleva to Kalevi, and inserted a derogatory insult calling him 'an old geezer manipulated by the Soviet Union'.
evidence: Minun mielestä se on Urho Kalevi Kekkonen eikö Urho Kaleva Kekkonen
value.claim_en: Urho Kekkonen's middle name was Kalevi and he was a senile old man controlled by the Soviet Union.
value.claim_fi: Urho Kekkosen toinen nimi oli Kalevi ja hän oli Neuvostoliiton ohjailema vanhus.
value.narrative_en: Anti-Kekkonen / Finlandization insult
value.historical_note_en: President Urho Kekkonen's official middle name was Kaleva, not Kalevi.
value.uncertainty_note: The input combines multiple consecutive reverted edits by different anonymous IPs into one diff (mixing sexual/nonsense graffiti, a derogatory political insult, and a seemingly confused edit changing 'Kaleva' to 'Kalevi' and back), though the dominant nature is clear vandalism.

value.what_changed_en: This grouped sequence of edits updated the COVID-19 statistics table for 25 May 2020, shifted prose about early cases from present to past tense (introducing typos like 'Naine' and 'tavoitetitin'), and removed a suspicious claim about a 'Professor Kalle Havumäki' that one editor noted linked to an unrelated joke article ('Muskrats ate Aake Kalliala's cottage pier'). However, the entire sequence of 7 edits was bulk-reverted to an earlier clean revision.
evidence: . Professori [[Kalle Havumäki]] oli tärkeässä roolissa todettujen tapausten diagnosoinnissa
linkkien takaa löytyy aivan muuta, kuten "Piisamit söivät Aake Kallialan mökkilaiturin"
value.claim_en: On 25 May 2020, Finland had 6,599 confirmed COVID-19 cases, 104 hospitalized, 18 in intensive care, and 308 deaths, and earlier patients had recovered.
value.claim_fi: Suomessa oli 25. toukokuuta 2020 todettu 6 599 koronavirustartuntaa, 104 sairaalahoidossa, 18 tehohoidossa ja 308 kuollutta, ja aiemmin sairastuneet potilaat olivat parantuneet.
value.uncertainty_note: The diff aggregates 7 edits by multiple editors (including IPs) that were reverted together. Some edits in the batch were constructive (updating the daily table, reverting a hoax about 'Kalle Havumäki'), while others introduced spelling mistakes, altered numbers (609 to 322), or may have left leftover vandalism from the sequence, prompting the bulk rollback.

value.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced entry for "freimit" (FPS, frames per second / frame rate) to the list of words of the decade. Another editor reverted it, arguing that frame rate is not particularly central to the 2020s as a whole.
evidence: Jos ajatellaan koko vuosikymmentä, niin kuvataajuus ei ole kovinkaan keskeinen
value.claim_en: The slang term "freimit" (frames per second / frame rate) is a notable word of the 2020s in Finland.
value.claim_fi: Sana "freimit" (FPS eli kuvataajuus) kuuluu 2020-luvun keskeisiin sanoihin Suomessa.
value.uncertainty_note: Could also be viewed as a minor content_dispute over list inclusion criteria, though adding an unsourced, older gaming term to a decade-words list best fits good_faith_error.

value.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced sentence stating that the popularity of basketball grew during the decade and that player Lauri Markkanen's career sparked interest in the sport among youth. The reverter removed it as unsourced and premature for characterizing an entire decade in 2022.
evidence: Vuosikymmenellä [[koripallo]]n suosio kasvoi ja koripalloilija [[Lauri Markkanen|Lauri Markkasen]] urheilu-ura herätti nuorissa kiinnostusta lajia kohtaan.
lähteetön ja perustelematon, katsellaan nyt pari vuotta, mihin suuntaan esim. pelaajalisenssien määrän kehitys menee, ja tuleeko tästä koko vuosikymmentä luonnehtiva trendi
value.claim_en: In the 2020s in Finland, the popularity of basketball grew and Lauri Markkanen's athletic career sparked interest in the sport among young people.
value.claim_fi: 2020-luvulla Suomessa koripallon suosio kasvoi ja Lauri Markkasen urheilu-ura herätti nuorissa kiinnostusta lajia kohtaan.

value.what_changed_en: Added sourced sentences about August COVID-19 rules for indoor gatherings under 500 people and restaurant seating, containing several spelling errors ('sisäkokoontumisisa', 'erityisä', 'mutat', 'eritysohjeet'). The edit was reverted within four minutes with the summary 'ei tietolähdettä' ('no source'), even though two web citations were included.
evidence: Alle 500 hengen sisäkokoontumisisa ei ole erityisä ehtoja, mutat hallitus suosittelee
Ravintoloissa on otettava huomioon tartuntatautilain eritysohjeet istumapaikkojen määristä, sijoitteluista ja ruuan tarjoilusta.
value.claim_en: Indoor gatherings of under 500 people have no special conditions beyond recommended hygiene and distancing guidelines, while restaurants must follow Communicable Diseases Act rules on seating and food service.
value.claim_fi: Alle 500 hengen sisäkokoontumisissa ei ole erityisiä ehtoja suositeltujen hygienia- ja turvaväliohjeiden lisäksi, ja ravintoloiden on noudatettava tartuntatautilain ohjeita istumapaikoista ja ruuan tarjoilusta.
value.uncertainty_note: The revert summary says 'ei tietolähdettä' (no source) despite two citations being present; the reverter may have misread the diff, objected to the typos and line breaks, or found that the sources did not verify the exact wording.

value.what_changed_en: Added a new section describing the cabinet's nickname 'huulipunahallitus' ('lipstick government') and its etymology, citing the Institute for the Languages of Finland (Kotus). The inserted text was accidentally duplicated with diff characters and copied verbatim from the source, prompting a revert for being unnecessary and a copyright violation.
evidence: Marinin hallituksen lempinimi on huulpunahallitus, jota voi pitää lempi- tai pilkkanimenä.
toivotaan, ettei käyttäjä [editor] ei sensuroi tätä faktaa pelkällä mielipiteensä vuoksi.
value.claim_en: Sanna Marin's cabinet is nicknamed 'huulipunahallitus' (lipstick government), a play on 'punamultahallitus' (red-earth government) that can be seen as an affectionate or derogatory reference to its female majority.
value.claim_fi: Sanna Marinin hallituksen lempinimi on huulipunahallitus, joka on väännös punamultahallituksesta ja jota voi pitää naisenemmistöön viittaavana lempi- tai pilkkanimenä.
value.uncertainty_note: The edit combines a content dispute over whether to include the nickname (evidenced by the editor's complaint about 'censorship' and the 'tarpeeton' revert) with policy/formatting errors (verbatim copy-pasting from Kotus and Wiktionary causing a copyright violation, plus accidental duplication). Could arguably fit good_faith_error or pov_push if the editor was trying to highlight a derogatory nickname.

value.what_changed_en: Added two sentences (with spelling errors like 'tarveysviranomaiset' and 'maaliskususa') stating that the government and health authorities imposed restrictions in March that were gradually lifted, and that the government discussed lifting the Emergency Powers Act on June 15, along with a Yle citation. Reverted with the summary 'ei tietolähdettä' ('no source'), likely referring to the unsourced first sentence or a follow-up edit.
evidence: Hallitus ja tarveysviranomaiset asettivat maaliskususa monia rajoituksia, joita on asteittain purettu epidemian hieman hellitettyä.
value.claim_en: The Finnish government and health authorities imposed many restrictions in March that have been gradually lifted as the epidemic eased slightly, and on June 15 the government discussed lifting the Emergency Powers Act.
value.claim_fi: Hallitus ja terveysviranomaiset asettivat maaliskuussa monia rajoituksia, joita on asteittain purettu epidemian hieman hellitettyä, ja 15. kesäkuuta hallitus keskusteli valmiuslain purkamisesta.
value.uncertainty_note: The revert summary says 'ei tietolähdettä' (no source) even though a Yle citation was included for the second sentence; the reverter may have objected to the unsourced first sentence, the typos, or reverted a batch of edits by the same IP.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted a paragraph into the lead section arguing that COVID-19 in Finland has not met the criteria for a mild pandemic (3,450 deaths in 8 weeks), synthesising a 2012 national influenza preparedness plan with current COVID-19 death statistics. Despite claiming in the edit summary to have removed the unsourced assertion that it was 'treated as a pandemic', the editor accidentally left that sentence in while duplicating the rest of the claim.
evidence: Koronaviruspandemiaa on kohdeltu pandemiana vaikka se ei ole täyttänyt [[Suomen sosiaali- ja terveysministeriö|sosiaali- ja terveysministeriön]] määrittämiä lievän pandemian tunnusmerkkejä, joissa 8 viikon tarkastelujaksolla koko maassa on 3450 kuolemantapausta.
viitteeksi merkitty julkaisu on vuodelta 2012, sillä tuskin voi lähteistää, miten koronapandemiaa on kohdeltu.
value.claim_en: The COVID-19 pandemic in Finland has not met the Finnish Ministry of Social Affairs and Health's criteria for even a mild pandemic, which requires 3,450 deaths over an eight-week period.
value.claim_fi: Koronaviruspandemia ei ole Suomessa täyttänyt sosiaali- ja terveysministeriön määrittämiä lievän pandemian tunnusmerkkejä, joihin kuuluu 3 450 kuolemantapausta kahdeksan viikon tarkastelujaksolla.
value.narrative_en: COVID-19 pandemic minimisation / scepticism
value.uncertainty_note: Also strongly overlaps with source_manipulation (original synthesis using a 2012 influenza scenario model as if it were a binding definition for COVID-19), which is what the reverting editor highlighted.

value.what_changed_en: Updated the date of the 2021 municipal elections from 18 April to 13 June without a source, and added an informal statement that the elections were originally to be held earlier 'but the Ministry of Justice changed its mind' ("mutta oikeusministeriö muutti mielipidettään").
value.claim_en: The 2021 Finnish municipal elections were moved from 18 April to 13 June 2021 because the Ministry of Justice changed its mind.
value.claim_fi: Vuoden 2021 kuntavaalit siirrettiin 18. huhtikuuta 13. kesäkuuta 2021 pidettäviksi, koska oikeusministeriö muutti mielipidettään.
value.historical_note_en: On 6 March 2021, party secretaries agreed to propose postponing the elections to 13 June due to the COVID-19 pandemic, though formal parliamentary legislation was still required rather than the Ministry of Justice unilaterally changing its mind.
value.uncertainty_note: The phrasing 'changed its mind' ('muutti mielipidettään') could either be clumsy/colloquial wording by an inexperienced editor trying to report breaking news on 6 March 2021, or mild editorialising/POV criticism of the postponement decision.

value.what_changed_en: The editor rewrote the description of how the Koronavilkku contact-tracing app works, claiming it uploads a list of nearby apps to a backend system, while accidentally mangling existing citation tags and deleting information about language and platform availability. The edit was reverted specifically for breaking the references.
evidence: Palautetaan viimeisin versio missä viitteitä ei ole sotkettu.
Sovellus lähettää taustajärjestelmälle tiedot lähellä olleiksi rekisteröimistänsä sovelluksista ja taustajärjedtelmä viestittää lähellä olleille sovelluksille, mahdollisesta altistumisesta.
value.claim_en: Koronavilkku keeps a log of nearby app instances, offers complete anonymity, and when an infected user enters a code from healthcare, the app sends data about nearby apps to a backend system that notifies them of possible exposure.
value.claim_fi: Koronavilkku pitää kirjaa lähietäisyydellä olleista sovelluksista, tarjoaa täyden anonymiteetin ja tartunnan saaneen syöttäessä koodin sovellus lähettää taustajärjestelmälle tiedot lähellä olleista sovelluksista, joille taustajärjestelmä viestittää mahdollisesta altistumisesta.
value.uncertainty_note: The technical description added by the editor is also inaccurate (decentralized DP-3T/GAEN apps upload the infected user's own temporary keys rather than a list of encountered devices, and the matching happens locally on devices rather than the backend messaging specific nearby apps), which could point toward false_factual_claim, but the broken wikitext citations and typos clearly indicate an earnest, clumsy attempt to clarify how the app works.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted unsourced commentary arguing that the Finnish Jägers committed treason and attempted a coup against Finland's lawful monarch (the Russian Emperor), and questioning the legality of Finland's 1917 declaration of independence. Also contained false claims, such as asserting that the death penalty was illegal in the Russian Empire for Christian reasons.
evidence: täten miehet syyllistyivät maanpetokseen. Tärkeää tässä nimenomaan on se, että miehet lähtivät vallankaappauksen tielle
valvoivat vallankaappauksellista, isänmaanvastaista ja laitonta liikehdintää.
Kuolemantuomio, joka monissa maissa oli yleinen tuomio vastaavanlaisesta petturuudesta, oli jääkärien onneksi laiton Venäjällä.
Eduskunnan itsenäisyysjulistus ei täyttänyt tätä laillista vaatimusta
value.claim_en: The Finnish Jägers were unpatriotic coup plotters guilty of treason against the lawful Grand Duke of Finland, and the legality of Finland's 1917 declaration of independence and the 1918 White government was questionable.
value.claim_fi: Jääkärit olivat isänmaanvastaisia vallankaappaajia, jotka syyllistyivät maanpetokseen Suomen laillista suuriruhtinasta vastaan, ja Suomen vuoden 1917 itsenäisyysjulistuksen sekä vuoden 1918 hallituksen laillisuus oli kyseenalainen.
value.narrative_en: Anti-Jäger / Tsarist legitimist framing of Finnish independence and the 1918 Civil War
value.historical_note_en: While seeking military training in Germany during WWI was indeed high treason under Russian imperial law, capital punishment was not abolished in the Russian Empire during WWI (especially for military treason), even though in practice captured Jäger activists imprisoned at Shpalernaya were not executed before the 1917 revolution freed them.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted an unsourced paragraph containing typos and stray quotation marks, arguing that the Hetemäki working group report overestimated COVID-19 prevalence and underestimated its lethality, meaning herd immunity was far away. The reverter removed it as unsourced opinionating.
evidence: Hetemäen raportti olettaa esimerkiksi, että korona olisis melko suurelle osalla väestöstä.
korona on raportin olettavaa tappavampi, ja laumasuoja hyvin kaukana.
value.claim_en: The Hetemäki report overestimates COVID-19 prevalence in Finland—which in reality is under one percent—making the virus deadlier than assumed and herd immunity distant.
value.claim_fi: Hetemäen raportti yliarvioi koronatartuntojen yleisyyden Suomessa, sillä todellisuudessa tartunnan saaneita on alle prosentti väestöstä, tauti on oletettua tappavampi ja laumasuoja on kaukana.
value.narrative_en: Criticism of early Finnish COVID-19 prevalence estimates and lockdown exit strategy
value.uncertainty_note: The stray opening quote mark suggests the editor might have intended to copy or paraphrase a published expert critique of the May 2020 Hetemäki report without attributing it, blurring the line between pov_push and good_faith_error (unsourced editorializing).

value.what_changed_en: Added general statements about COVID-19 symptoms (describing it as deadly to risk groups though usually mild and flu-like), hygiene advice, border closures, and economic impacts with a Helsingin Sanomat citation. The edit was reverted for adding unsourced claims.
evidence: Koronavirus on riskiryhmille tappava tauti, vaikka on yleensä vain lievä influessaa muistuttava.
Rajat suljettiin. THL kehotti pitämään etäisyyttä ihmisiin ja pesemään käsiä mm. ulkoa tultaessa
value.claim_en: COVID-19 is a deadly disease for risk groups although usually mild and flu-like, and the pandemic led to border closures, hygiene recommendations, and economic harm including unemployment.
value.claim_fi: Koronavirus on riskiryhmille tappava mutta yleensä lievä influenssaa muistuttava tauti, ja pandemia johti rajojen sulkemiseen, hygieniaohjeisiin sekä talousvaikeuksiin ja työttömyyteen.
value.uncertainty_note: The phrase comparing COVID-19 to a mild flu could be seen as mildly downplaying the virus, and describing sectors as suffering from 'countermeasures' rather than the pandemic itself carries slight framing, making 'content_dispute' a plausible alternative, though overall it reads like an earnest summary attempt with a citation.

value.what_changed_en: Prematurely updated the article on election night (2 April 2023) to state that Sanna Marin's term as Prime Minister ended on that date and that Petteri Orpo succeeded her. In Finland, the outgoing government continues in office until the new cabinet is formally appointed after coalition negotiations.
evidence: Petteri Orpo on nyt Suomen uusi pääministeri
value.claim_en: Sanna Marin's term as Prime Minister of Finland ended on 2 April 2023, when Petteri Orpo became the new Prime Minister.
value.claim_fi: Sanna Marinin toimikausi Suomen pääministerinä päättyi 2. huhtikuuta 2023, jolloin Petteri Orposta tuli uusi pääministeri.
value.historical_note_en: Following the 2 April 2023 parliamentary election, Sanna Marin continued serving as Prime Minister until Petteri Orpo's cabinet was formally appointed on 20 June 2023.
value.uncertainty_note: Could also be viewed as false_factual_claim, though it is clearly a common good-faith misunderstanding of constitutional procedure on election night rather than deliberate misinformation.

value.what_changed_en: Changed the spelling of "social democrats" and "social democratic" throughout the article from the standard Finnish spelling with a double 'a' ("sosiaalidemokraatit") to the single-'a' spelling used in the party's official name ("sosialidemokraatit"). The reverter noted that the Institute for the Languages of Finland (Kotus) recommends the double-'a' spelling in general text.
evidence: Kotuksen suositus on, että kirjoitetaan 2:lla a:lla, vaikka puolue kirjoittaa yhdellä

value.what_changed_en: Changed the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases in Finland on 17 March 2020 from 322 to 609, broke the sentence formatting, and inserted a joke claim that 'Professor Kalle Havumäki played an important role in diagnosing the confirmed cases' (Havumäki is a Finnish musician with developmental disabilities, not a medical professor), under the edit summary 'update'.
evidence: Professori [[Kalle Havumäki]] oli tärkeässä roolissa todettujen tapausten diagnosoinnissa
value.claim_en: On 17 March 2020 Finland had 609 confirmed coronavirus cases and Professor Kalle Havumäki played an important role in diagnosing them.
value.claim_fi: 17. maaliskuuta 2020 Suomessa oli 609 todettua koronavirustartuntaa ja professori Kalle Havumäki oli tärkeässä roolissa niiden diagnosoinnissa.
value.historical_note_en: Kalle Havumäki is the singer of the Finnish punk band Resisposse, not a medical professor involved in COVID-19 diagnostics.

value.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced claim that the first Finns contracted COVID-19 at the Military World Games in Wuhan in November 2019 and subsequently infected family members in Finland that same month, noting that authorities have not announced this. It also left an orphaned word fragment ('oireyhtymään', meaning 'to the syndrome') on a new line, and was reverted for lacking a source.
evidence: Ensimmäiset suomalaiset saivat COVID-19 tartunnan Kiinan Wuhanissa marraskuussa 2019 järjestetyissä sotilaiden maailmanmestaruuskisoissa.
Asiasta ei kuitenkaan ole toistaiseksi tiedotettu, vaikka myös heidän perheenjäseniään sairaustui COVID-19 Suomessa jo marraskuussa 2019.
value.claim_en: The first Finns contracted COVID-19 at the Military World Games in Wuhan in November 2019 and transmitted it to family members in Finland that same month, without public disclosure.
value.claim_fi: Ensimmäiset suomalaiset saivat COVID-19-tartunnan Wuhanin sotilaiden maailmanmestaruuskisoissa marraskuussa 2019 ja tartuttivat perheenjäseniään Suomessa jo samassa kuussa ilman julkista tiedotusta.
value.narrative_en: COVID-19 spread in Europe via the 2019 Wuhan Military World Games and was kept quiet by authorities
value.historical_note_en: The 2019 Military World Games in Wuhan were held in October 2019 (not November), and Finland's first confirmed COVID-19 case was recorded in late January 2020.
value.uncertainty_note: The editor may have sincerely believed personal rumours or anecdotal reports (which existed among European athletes from the October 2019 Wuhan games), putting this near the boundary between false_factual_claim and good_faith_error (original research).

value.what_changed_en: Reordered the list of Sanna Marin's Deputy Prime Ministers in the infobox, adding numbering (1. and 2.) and inaccurate term dates for Annika Saarikko and Katri Kulmuni while framing Matti Vanhanen as second deputy. The revert summary cited the edit as unsourced and added by an untrustworthy user.
value.claim_en: Annika Saarikko became Sanna Marin's first Deputy Prime Minister on 10 September 2020, directly succeeding Katri Kulmuni, with Matti Vanhanen serving as second deputy.
value.claim_fi: Annika Saarikko toimi Sanna Marinin ensimmäisenä sijaisena 10.9.2020 alkaen Katri Kulmunin jälkeen ja Matti Vanhanen toisena sijaisena.
value.historical_note_en: Katri Kulmuni stepped down as Deputy Prime Minister in June 2020 and was succeeded by Matti Vanhanen until September 2020, when Annika Saarikko became the sole official Deputy Prime Minister.
value.uncertainty_note: The revert summary notes an 'untrustworthy user' (likely a sockpuppet or notorious subtle hoaxer), meaning this could be deliberate subtle misinformation (false_factual_claim) rather than an honest mistake about ministerial substitution rules.

value.what_changed_en: Ended Krista Kiuru's term as Minister of Family Affairs and Social Services on 27 January 2022 and added Hanna Sarkkinen as her successor in the cabinet table, with an explanatory footnote and source stating that Sarkkinen was acting in the role during Kiuru's sick leave. The edit was reverted because Sarkkinen was only deputising for Kiuru rather than being formally appointed to the portfolio.
evidence: Hanna Sarkkinen toimii perhe- ja peruspalveluministerinä Krista Kiurun sairausloman ajan.
Sarkkista ei ole nimitetty perhe- ja peruspalveluministeriksi, hän vain sijaistaa Kiurua
value.claim_en: Hanna Sarkkinen succeeded Krista Kiuru as Minister of Family Affairs and Social Services on 27 January 2022 for the duration of Kiuru's sick leave.
value.claim_fi: Hanna Sarkkinen aloitti perhe- ja peruspalveluministerinä Krista Kiurun tilalla 27. tammikuuta 2022 Kiurun sairausloman ajaksi.

value.what_changed_en: Added a new subsection for September 17 stating that the Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL) did not recommend traveling outside Europe, citing a Helsingin Sanomat news article from the same day. The reverter rejected the edit because the added text did not match what the cited source said.
evidence: THL ei suositellut Euroopan ulkopuolele matkustamista.
nimeke=Koronavirus {{!}} THL: Koronavirustapaukset ovat lisääntyneet huolestuttavasti, tilanne lähestyy kiihtymisvaihetta
value.claim_en: On September 17, 2020, the Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL) did not recommend traveling outside Europe.
value.claim_fi: THL ei suositellut matkustamista Euroopan ulkopuolelle 17. syyskuuta 2020.
value.uncertainty_note: Without reading the full text of the cited Helsingin Sanomat article, it is unclear whether the editor sincerely misread the article (good_faith_error) or deliberately misrepresented it (source_manipulation / false_factual_claim), though the typo 'ulkopuolele' and proper citation formatting suggest a rushed good-faith news update.

value.what_changed_en: Added a sentence describing official guidelines from THL and the Ministry of Education and Culture (OKM) regarding high-risk group hobbies during the COVID-19 pandemic, citing an Ilta-Sanomat news article using a bare external link instead of a proper citation tag. The edit was reverted due to the formatting policy against placing bare external links in the body text.
evidence: THL:n ja OKM:n ohjeiden mukaan tartuntariski on korkea varsinkin
poistetaan koko lisäys, ei ulkoista linkkiä leipätekstiin

value.what_changed_en: Replaced instances of 'valtio' (state) with 'suuriruhtinaskunta' (grand duchy) and 'valtiopäivät' (state diet) with 'maapäivät' (provincial diet). The editor argued in the summary that Finland was not a state between 1809 and 1917 because it lacked sovereignty, while the reverting editor asserted it was a state.

value.claim_en: Finland was not a state between 1809 and 1917 because it was not a sovereign entity, and its legislative assembly was a provincial diet rather than a state diet.
value.claim_fi: Suomi ei ollut valtio vuosina 1809–1917, koska se ei ollut suvereeni yksikkö, ja sen säätykokous oli luonteeltaan maapäivät eikä valtiopäivät.
value.narrative_en: Historiographical debate over whether autonomous Finland (1809–1917) constituted a state
value.uncertainty_note: In Finnish historiography, whether the Grand Duchy was a 'valtio' (state) from 1809 and whether the Diet of Porvoo should be called 'valtiopäivät' or 'maapäivät' is a genuine, classic scholarly debate (e.g., Osmo Jussila vs. older nationalist historiography). Because this reflects a legitimate historiographical disagreement rather than fringe ideological spin, 'content_dispute' fits slightly better than 'pov_push', though unilaterally rewriting terminology across an article leans toward pushing a specific historiographical POV.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced multiple historical terms, dates, and names throughout the introduction with juvenile obscenities, homophobic remarks, and nonsensical dates (for example, changing "1899 February Manifesto" to "4729 May penis" and "military" to "gay people"). value.claim_en: Swedish-speaking officials failed to learn Finnish after the 1863 language decree, Russia issued the 1902 decree to improve the position of Finnish, and in 1906 state administration remained entirely Swedish-speaking, preventing Finns from participating in governance.
value.claim_fi: Ruotsinkieliset virkamiehet eivät opetelleet suomea vuoden 1863 kieliasetuksen siirtymäajan kuluessa, Venäjä antoi vuoden 1902 asetuksen suomen aseman parantamiseksi ja vuonna 1906 valtionhallinto oli edelleen täysin ruotsinkielistä estäen suomalaisten osallistumisen hallintoon.

value.uncertainty_note: The edit combines strong nationalist/Fennoman POV framing, historically inaccurate generalizations (e.g., calling administration 'entirely Swedish-speaking' in 1906 when the unicameral parliament wasn't even elected until 1907 and citing a 1908 petition), and source manipulation (leaving the Pulma 2003b / Olkkonen 2003 citation attached to rewritten text that no longer reflects those historians, as noted by the reverter); false_factual_claim or source_manipulation are close secondary fits.

value.what_changed_en: Changed the neutral verb 'luovutti' (ceded) to 'joutui luovuttamaan' (was forced to cede) regarding Finland's WWII territorial losses, added geographic details and wikilinks about the ceded areas (such as Rybachy and Sredny peninsulas and Inari), changed a 19th-century border adjustment year from 1866 to 1864, and altered minor wording.
value.claim_en: Finland was forced to cede over half of Finnish Karelia, eastern Salla and Kuusamo, and northeastern Petsamo in 1940, was forced to cede further territory in 1944 and sell part of Inari in 1947, and had an autonomy-era border adjustment in 1864 rather than 1866.
value.claim_fi: Suomi joutui luovuttamaan Neuvostoliitolle alueita vuosina 1940 ja 1944 sekä myymään alueen Inarista vuonna 1947, ja autonomian ajan rajajärjestely tapahtui vuonna 1864 eikä 1866.
value.narrative_en: Emphasising the involuntary nature of Finnish territorial cessions to the Soviet Union
value.uncertainty_note: The edit combines accurate geographic elaboration and wikilinks with slightly non-neutral framing ('was forced to cede' instead of 'ceded') and an unsourced date change next to a cited paragraph (the Siestarjoki transfer happened in 1864, though demarcation or other steps may explain 1866 in the source). Because the revert gave no reason and reverted within 5 minutes, it could also be classified as a content_dispute or a routine revert of a known sockpuppet/block-evading IP.

value.what_changed_en: The editor reverted to a preferred version of the article, restoring coat of arms images and redefining the historical and modern divisions of Karelia—specifically equating East Karelia strictly with the Republic of Karelia, mapping its modern districts one-to-one onto historical regions (including a coined 'Puutoisten Karjala' for Pudozh), and claiming Border Karelia was detached from Olonets Karelia in the Treaty of Stolbovo. They also removed a citation-needed tag and placed scare quotes around 'independent' when referring to the Karelian-Finnish SSR.
evidence: Itä-Karjala = Karjalan Tasavalta = Venäjän Karjala Länsi-Karjala = Karjalan historiallinen maakunta = Suomen Karjala
value.claim_en: East Karelia is synonymous with the Republic of Karelia, whose modern administrative districts correspond directly to historical Karelian subregions including 'Puutoisten Karjala', and Border Karelia was originally detached from Olonets Karelia in the 1617 Treaty of Stolbovo.
value.claim_fi: Itä-Karjala tarkoittaa samaa kuin Karjalan tasavalta, jonka nykyiset piirit vastaavat suoraan historiallisia osa-alueita kuten 'Puutoisten Karjalaa', ja Raja-Karjala irrotettiin alun perin Aunuksen Karjalasta Stolbovan rauhassa.
value.historical_note_en: In Finnish historical geography, East Karelia refers specifically to White Karelia (Viena) and Olonets Karelia (Aunus) rather than all of the modern Republic of Karelia (where the Pudozh district east of Lake Onega is historically Russian territory, not Karelian), and Border Karelia was part of Kexholm County ceded in 1617 rather than detached from Olonets.
value.uncertainty_note: Because the edit introduces idiosyncratic, unsourced historical-geographical definitions (such as 'Puutoisten Karjala' and exact district mappings), false_factual_claim is a close alternative to content_dispute, though it occurs within an ongoing multi-editor dispute over how to structure and define Karelia's subregions.

value.what_changed_en: Changed the neutral phrase 'Negotiations broke off' to 'The Soviet Union broke off the negotiations' (also breaking the link to the date 'November 9' due to a missing line break), and inserted an unsourced sentence stating that the Soviet government subsequently made repeated demands on the Baltic states leading to their annexation.
evidence: Tämän jälkeen Neuvostohallitus esitti baltian maiden hallituksille lisää vaatimuksia aina uudestaan ja uudestaan, johtaen lopulta näiden maiden liittämiseen osaksi Neuvostoliittoa.
value.claim_en: The Soviet Union unilaterally broke off the November 1939 Moscow negotiations with Finland and afterward repeatedly made escalating demands on the Baltic states that led to their annexation.
value.claim_fi: Neuvostoliitto katkaisi yksipuolisesti marraskuun 1939 Moskovan neuvottelut Suomen kanssa ja esitti tämän jälkeen toistuvasti uusia vaatimuksia Baltian maille, mikä johti niiden liittämiseen osaksi Neuvostoliittoa.
value.narrative_en: Emphasising Soviet aggression and linking Finland's pre-war negotiations to the occupation of the Baltic states
value.historical_note_en: During the 1939 Moscow negotiations neither side formally broke off talks on November 9—the Finnish delegation returned to Helsinki after reaching an impasse—and the initial Soviet mutual assistance pacts with the Baltic states had already been concluded in September–October 1939, prior to November 9, with full occupation occurring in June 1940.
value.uncertainty_note: The edit combines one-sided framing ('pov_push'), chronological/factual inaccuracies ('false_factual_claim'), and poor formatting/unsourced addition ('good_faith_error'); the reverter explicitly flagged it as unsourced and unjustified viewpoints ('lähteettömiä ja perustelemattomia näkökantoja').

value.claim_en: In May 1941, Finland's top leadership decided to participate in Germany's planned military campaign against the Soviet Union, setting conditions in early June that Finland remain independent, Germany attack first, and Finland enter the fighting only after Soviet hostilities began.

value.claim_fi: Argentiinan aloitteen ja Yhdistyneen kuningaskunnan alahuoneen keskustelun jälkeen Kansainliitto erotti Neuvostoliiton 14. joulukuuta 1939 Suomeen hyökkäämisen vuoksi, mitä Neuvostoliiton tiedotusvälineet pitivät Englannin ja Ranskan järjestämänä skandaalina.
