value.historical_note_en: Kekkonen took sick leave in September 1981 and announced his permanent incapacity on 26 October 1981, though Mauno Koivisto formally took office as his elected successor on 27 January 1982.
value.uncertainty_note: Because both summaries indicate reverts of different revision IDs by IP/mixed editors, this could be an incomplete anti-vandalism revert that restored an earlier disputed version, rather than a deliberate disagreement over how to date the end of Kekkonen's term.

value.what_changed_en: This edit attempted to revert prior vandalism that had changed Tarja Halonen's party affiliation to the Communist Party of Finland and claimed she had substance abuse problems, restoring her actual Social Democratic Party background and biographical text. It was reverted within a minute, likely due to an accidental double-revert or edit conflict among editors fighting vandalism.
value.claim_en: Tarja Halonen's party background is in the Social Democratic Party of Finland, and her stepfather Thure Herman Forss was an active labour movement representative who greatly influenced her life.
value.claim_fi: Tarja Halonen on puoluetaustaltaan sosiaalidemokraatti, ja hänen isäpuolensa Thure Herman Forss oli aktiivinen työväenliikkeen edustaja, jolla oli suuri vaikutus hänen elämäänsä.
value.uncertainty_note: The edit itself restored accurate text after IP vandalism; it was likely reverted either by accident (overlapping anti-vandalism reverts) or by the vandal returning. Without seeing who reverted it and the subsequent revision, it is unclear whether the reverter was a confused patroller or a vandal, though 'other' (tool/revert collision) best fits the edit itself.

value.what_changed_en: Deleted a large section about Kekkonen's childhood and youth, corrupted existing citations and templates, inserted random keyboard mashing, and duplicated a paragraph about his university years and early career.
evidence: Ogf ctsikko = Myös Kekkonen osallistui teloituksiin
value.uncertainty_note: Borders on test_or_nonsense due to keyboard mashing, but large-scale deletion and template corruption alongside a revert summary calling it vandalism place it firmly in vandalism.

value.what_changed_en: Removed documented facts about Tarja Halonen's past roles in the Committee for the Recognition of the GDR, opposition to the EEC trade agreement, and chairmanship of the LGBT rights organization SETA. Inserted exaggerated, satirical praise claiming she is the most popular president in Western history and blaming 'intolerant racists' supporting military figures for her not ranking higher in a poll, which reverter summaries identified as reverse-psychology trolling.
evidence: . Halonen on suosituin presidentti länsimaissa koskaan
Halonen olisi päässyt paljon paremmille sijoille, elleivät jotkut suvaitsemattomat rasistit olisi tukeneet sotilashenkilöitä.
Palautus. Käänteisyydelle perustuva Halosen vastainen politikointi läpäisee vain typerykset....
value.claim_en: Tarja Halonen is the most popular president in the history of Western countries and only ranked lower in polls because intolerant racists supported military figures.
value.claim_fi: Tarja Halonen on länsimaiden historian suosituin presidentti, joka jäi äänestyksissä alemmille sijoille vain siksi, että suvaitsemattomat rasistit tukivat sotilashenkilöitä.
value.narrative_en: Satirical or partisan caricature of Tarja Halonen ahead of the 2006 presidential election
value.uncertainty_note: On the surface the text looks like an extreme pro-Halonen pov_push, but the over-the-top hyperbole and the reverter's note about reverse-psychology politicking strongly point to deliberate satirical trolling (vandalism).

value.what_changed_en: Inserted an unsourced sentence into the 'Criticism' ('Kritiikkiä') section stating that Sanna Marin supports male-only conscription. The reverter removed it as unsourced and poorly placed ('lähteetön ja huonossa paikassa').
evidence: Sanna Marin kannattaa vain miehille suunnattua asevelvollisuutta.
value.claim_en: Sanna Marin supports conscription directed solely at men.
value.claim_fi: Sanna Marin kannattaa vain miehille suunnattua asevelvollisuutta.
value.narrative_en: Criticism of male-only conscription in Finland
value.uncertainty_note: Adding an unsourced statement about male-only conscription specifically under 'Criticism' suggests an intent to highlight a perceived double standard on gender equality (pov_push), though it also exhibits traits of a misplaced, unsourced addition (good_faith_error) or potentially an oversimplification of her political stance (false_factual_claim).

value.what_changed_en: Fixed a grammatical case error ('liiallista' to 'liiallisesta'), accidentally duplicated an existing lead paragraph, and inserted an unsourced paragraph praising Kekkonen as an internationally respected statesman at the peak of his career during the 1975 CSCE summit with a broken link to the Nobel Peace Prize. The reverter rejected the changes as unsourced personal opinion.
evidence: Joka tapauksessa hän oli kansainvälisestikin arvostettu valtiomies.
oli samana vuonna ehdolla Nobelin rauhanpalkinnon saajaksi.
ei tietolähdettä, arvelen, että kirjoittajan oma näkemys
value.claim_en: Despite criticism of excessive power, Kekkonen was an internationally respected statesman who reached the peak of his career in 1975 by hosting the CSCE in Helsinki and being nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize.
value.claim_fi: Vallankäyttöön kohdistuneesta kritiikistä huolimatta Kekkonen oli kansainvälisesti arvostettu valtiomies, joka oli uransa huipulla isännöidessään ETYK-kokousta vuonna 1975 ja ollessaan samana vuonna ehdolla Nobelin rauhanpalkinnon saajaksi.
value.narrative_en: Positive appraisal of Urho Kekkonen as an internationally respected statesman
value.uncertainty_note: Because the revert summary mentions reverting the last two edits together, this edit appears to fix a typo and wikilink in a paragraph added just prior while accidentally duplicating text; it also borders on pov_push due to defensive, admiring phrasing ('Joka tapauksessa hän oli kansainvälisestikin arvostettu valtiomies').

value.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced statement claiming that politician Paavo Väyrynen criticized Juha Sipilä's cabinet in speeches and a book, alleging that Laestadians (followers of preacher Lars Levi Laestadius) took power in the party and allied with the country's far-right. The editor re-inserted this material in an edit war, complaining in the summary about the removal of a 'fact'.
evidence: Paavo Väyrynen on arvostellut sekä puheissaan että kirjassaan Juha sipilän hallitusta
lestadiolaisten eli pajalalaisen saarnamiehen Lars Levi Laestadiuksen kannattajien ottaneen puolueessa vallan ja liittoutuneen maan äärioikeiston kanssa.
Meni noin monta minuuttia poistaa tosiasia.
value.claim_en: Paavo Väyrynen has criticized Juha Sipilä's cabinet by alleging that Laestadians took power in the Centre Party and allied with Finland's far-right.
value.claim_fi: Paavo Väyrynen on arvostellut Juha Sipilän hallitusta esittäen lestadiolaisten ottaneen vallan puolueessa ja liittoutuneen maan äärioikeiston kanssa.
value.narrative_en: Criticism of Juha Sipilä's religious background and his coalition with the Finns Party
value.uncertainty_note: It is possible Väyrynen made similar remarks, which would make this primarily an unsourced undue-weight issue (good_faith_error or content_dispute), though the edit-warring summary and pointed framing regarding Laestadians and the 'far-right' strongly point to POV pushing.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted a joke sentence claiming that Sanna Marin has continuously been the best-looking politician in the world for nearly 500 days, mimicking the preceding sentence about her days in office. The editor also used the undo tool to restore this previously reverted vandalism.
evidence: Sanna Marin on tällä hetkellä ollut yhtäjaksoisesti lähes 500 vuorokautta maailman hyvännäköisin poliitikko.
value.claim_en: Sanna Marin has continuously been the best-looking politician in the world for nearly 500 days.
value.claim_fi: Sanna Marin on ollut yhtäjaksoisesti lähes 500 vuorokautta maailman hyvännäköisin poliitikko.

value.what_changed_en: An editor reverted vandalism ('antero pinokkio'), restoring an earlier unsourced addition by IP 84.249.x.x about President Tarja Halonen reappointing her party colleague Ritva Viljanen to the Ministry of the Interior against the government's unanimous proposal of a person deemed more qualified (plus a stray 'Tarja Kaarina'). The community then reverted that restored addition because it lacked sources.
evidence: puoluetoverinsa [[Ritva Viljanen|Ritva Viljasen]], jälkimmäisellä kerralla vastoin hallitusta, joka oli yksimielisesti ehdottanut pätevämmäksi katsottua henkilöä.
value.claim_en: Tarja Halonen appointed her party colleague Ritva Viljanen as Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of the Interior in 2003 and again in 2008, the second time against a government that had unanimously proposed a person considered more qualified.
value.claim_fi: Tarja Halonen nimitti puoluetoverinsa Ritva Viljasen sisäasiainministeriön kansliapäälliköksi vuonna 2003 ja uudelleen vuonna 2008 vastoin hallitusta, joka oli yksimielisesti ehdottanut pätevämmäksi katsottua henkilöä.
value.narrative_en: Criticism of Tarja Halonen for partisan political appointments
value.uncertainty_note: This edit is a coupled edit: a vandalism revert that inadvertently restored a prior unsourced, slightly POV-framed edit (along with the stray fragment 'Tarja Kaarina'). Depending on whether one classifies the vandal-reverter's action or the underlying restored text, 'pov_push' would also fit.

value.what_changed_en: Added daily COVID-19 statistics for April 27 (4,695 infections, 187 hospitalized, 56 in intensive care, and 193 dead) with a minor typo ('tehohoissa' instead of 'tehohoidossa'), copying the named citation tag from the previous day's entry. It was reverted because the reused reference was originally dated March 12, 2020, and did not match or verify the newly added April 27 figures.
evidence: '''27. huhtikuuta''' 4695 tartuntaa. 187 sairaalassa, joista 56 tehohoissa. 193 kuollut.
tietolähde päivätty 12.3.2020 ja tieto on lisätty 27.4., lisätty tieto ei ole lähteen mukainen
value.claim_en: On April 27, 2020, Finland had recorded 4,695 COVID-19 cases, 187 hospitalized patients (including 56 in intensive care), and 193 deaths.
value.claim_fi: 27. huhtikuuta 2020 Suomessa oli todettu 4 695 koronavirustartuntaa, sairaalahoidossa oli 187 potilasta (joista 56 tehohoidossa) ja kuolleita oli 193.
value.uncertainty_note: The editor clearly copied the markup pattern from the April 26 entry (which also used <ref name=":61" />, likely a live-updating news blog originally launched on March 12) without updating the citation access date or providing a proper standalone source, making this a textbook good-faith sourcing mistake rather than intentional source manipulation.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted an unsourced claim stating that thousands of people had already died of COVID-19 in Finland by March 2020, accompanied by a profane edit summary ("Vitun aars", roughly "Fucking aars/SARS").
evidence: Oikeasti siihen on Suomessa kuollut jo tuhansia ihmisiä.
value.claim_en: Thousands of people had already died of COVID-19 in Finland by mid-March 2020.
value.claim_fi: Suomessa oli kuollut koronavirukseen jo tuhansia ihmisiä maaliskuun 2020 puoliväliin mennessä.
value.narrative_en: COVID-19 death toll cover-up or exaggeration
value.historical_note_en: Finland recorded its very first confirmed COVID-19 death on 20 March 2020, three days after this edit was made.
value.uncertainty_note: The profane edit summary ('Vitun aars') suggests deliberate trolling or vandalism, making this a borderline case between 'false_factual_claim' and 'vandalism'.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted stray characters and typos into the infobox, an image filename, and citation tags, breaking formatting, and changed the bolded lead name '''Sanna to "neitiSanna" ("MissSanna").
value.uncertainty_note: The stray letters ('ä', 'v') look like careless typing or a test edit, while 'neitiSanna' ('MissSanna') looks like mild mockery or deliberate graffiti, straddling vandalism and test_or_nonsense.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced a sourced paragraph about Sanna Marin's political career with raw copy-pasted text from the Finnish Bible website (Raamattu.fi), including navigation menus and the beginning of the Gospel of Matthew. The edit summary misleadingly claimed to add information about Marin's history, political stances, and ideologies.
evidence: Jeesuksen Kristuksen, Daavidin pojan ja Abrahamin pojan, sukuluettelo:
Lisäsin paljon lisää tietoa Marinin historiasta ja politiikan kannanotoista sekä aatteista

value.what_changed_en: Inserted an unsourced sentence into the 'Personal life' section claiming that two days before the parliamentary elections, the online magazine Egorazzi announced it possessed a sex tape of Sanna Marin and intended to publish it the day before the elections.
evidence: Kaksi päivää ennen eduskuntavaaleja, Egorazzi-lehti ilmoitti sillä olevan hallusaan Sanna Marinin seksivideo, jonka se aikoo julkaista päivää ennen vaaleja.
value.claim_en: Two days before the 2023 Finnish parliamentary elections, the magazine Egorazzi announced it possessed a sex tape of Sanna Marin to be released the day before the elections.
value.claim_fi: Kaksi päivää ennen eduskuntavaaleja Egorazzi-lehti ilmoitti pitävänsä hallussaan Sanna Marinin seksivideota, jonka se aikoi julkaista päivää ennen vaaleja.
value.narrative_en: Pre-election scandalmongering against Sanna Marin
value.uncertainty_note: Egorazzi is a notorious Finnish tabloid/men's site known for clickbait and April Fools' stunts (the edit was made on March 31, two days before the April 2, 2023 election, making 'the day before the election' April 1). Depending on whether the site actually published this hoax announcement, the edit could also be classified as a false_factual_claim, pov_push, or good_faith_error by an editor falling for tabloid bait, though inserting unsourced sex-tape rumors into a biography of a living person right before an election strongly resembles vandalism or smear.

value.what_changed_en: Added an unsourced, unpunctuated sentence to the 'Personal life' section claiming that Sanna Marin had been dating hairdresser Joni Willberg since May 2023, broke up briefly in September 2023, and resumed the relationship a month later. The edit was reverted for lacking a source and encyclopedic relevance.
evidence: Marin on seurustellut toukokuusta 2023 lähtien parturi kampaaja joni willbergin kanssa
he erosivat hetkeksi syyskuussa 2023 mutta jatkoivat seurustelua jo kuukauden kuluttua
Ei lähdettä, eikä edes tarpeellinen tieto Wikipediassa.
value.claim_en: Sanna Marin has been dating hairdresser Joni Willberg since May 2023, with a brief breakup in September 2023.
value.claim_fi: Sanna Marin on seurustellut parturi-kampaaja Joni Willbergin kanssa toukokuusta 2023 lähtien, lukuun ottamatta lyhyttä eroa syyskuussa 2023.
value.uncertainty_note: Finnish tabloids did circulate gossip rumours about Marin and Joni Willberg in 2023 before they were confirmed later on, so while the claim lacked reliable verification at the time (bordering on false_factual_claim under BLP rules), it appears to be a sincere attempt by an inexperienced user to add tabloid news rather than deliberate fabrication or malice.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced multiple biographical details in Sanna Marin's personal life section—such as her family, husband, residence in Tampere, and vegetarianism—with insults,
evidence: Sanna Marin on täys rasisti ketä pitäis heittää kalliolta ales. Hän on myös pölliny venäjältä mopoja.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted a poorly formatted, misspelled summary essay of the Winter War at the bottom of the article, signed 'made by : best person ---matias---'. The reverter removed it suspecting a copyright violation, though it strongly resembles a pasted school essay duplicating existing article content.
value.uncertainty_note: The closing signature ('best person ---matias---') has a playful/graffiti element, and the reverter suspected a copyright violation (probably a student paraphrasing a textbook), making it borderline between good_faith_error and minor vandalism/other.

value.what_changed_en: Alongside updating the daily COVID-19 case and death statistics with citations, the editor inserted a vandalistic sentence claiming that "some 16000000000000 people" had died in Finland and wrote "Kakka" ("Poop") in the edit summary.
evidence: Sen vuoksi on Suomessa kuollut jo kotqin 16000000000000 ihmistä.
value.claim_en: Some 16 trillion people have died in Finland due to COVID-19.
value.claim_fi: Suomessa on kuollut koronaviruksen vuoksi jo jokin 16 000 000 000 000 ihmistä.
value.uncertainty_note: The diff appears to combine a genuine statistical update with blatant vandalism (possibly because the diff spans or reverts multiple edits at once, as hinted by the revert summary reverting 2 edits).

value.what_changed_en: Expanded a short summary section on COVID-19 epidemic forecasts and models with several sourced paragraphs detailing models from THL, Aalto University, the REINA group, and the Hetemäki report, along with criticisms of their accuracy. Another editor reverted the two consecutive edits because this detailed material belonged in the dedicated sub-article ('tämä kuuluu pääartikkeliin').
evidence: THL julkaisi maaliskuun lopussa mallin, jonka pohjalta koronavirusepidemian 1. aalto olisi kestänyt kevään ja kesän yli sekä vienyt sairaalaan tuhansia suomalaisia
Kriitikoiden mukaan tämänkin mallin pohjaoletuksissa on paljon vikaa, eikä sillä kyetä ennustamaan epidemian kulkua luotettavasti.
value.claim_en: Various Finnish COVID-19 epidemic models published in spring 2020 predicted differing hospitalization and mortality outcomes, failed to materialize as projected in several ways, and faced criticism regarding their underlying assumptions.
value.claim_fi: Keväällä 2020 julkaistut suomalaiset koronavirusepidemiamallit ennustivat erilaisia sairaalahoidon ja kuolleisuuden määriä, eivät toteutuneet monin tavoin ennustetusti ja saivat osakseen kritiikkiä pohjaoletuksistaan.
value.uncertainty_note: The diff compares against an earlier intermediate edit by the same anonymous editor (since the revert rolled back 2 edits at once). Some of the phrasing synthesizing model failures ('Malli ei toteutunut monellakaan tavoin') leans slightly toward editorializing or original synthesis, so content_dispute is a minor alternative, though the explicit reason for reversion was article structure/misplacement.

value.what_changed_en: Translated English labels in the COVID-19 case chart into Finnish, updated case counts (adding an entry for January 26 and changing 30 to 33), and added a sentence with four news citations stating that Finland began preparing for a wider epidemic in late February. The edit was reverted as part of a batch of six edits for adding trivia and over-citing.
evidence: Suomikin varautui mahdolliseen tulevaan laajempaan epidemiaan jo helmikuun lopussa
value.claim_en: Finland began preparing for a potential wider coronavirus epidemic at the end of February 2020, had a recorded case on January 26, and reached 33 cases.
value.claim_fi: Suomi varautui mahdolliseen laajempaan koronavirusepidemiaan jo helmikuun 2020 lopussa, ja maassa todettiin tapaus 26. tammikuuta sekä yhteensä 33 tapausta.
value.uncertainty_note: The revert summary explicitly mentions reverting 6 consecutive edits for 'trivia, over-citing' ('triviaa, yliviitteistystä'), so this could also be seen as a minor content_dispute over style and citation density rather than purely a good_faith_error.

value.what_changed_en: Added two sourced sentences (with minor typos) about the start of domestic production of hospital-grade masks and respirators in Finland in late May 2020. The reverter undid the edit, calling the use of the word 'maski' (mask) instead of 'hengityssuojain' (respirator) for healthcare professionals' equipment misleading, even though the cited news headlines used 'maski'.
evidence: 26. toukokuuta suomalainen yritys oli käynnistänyt sairaalatasojen maskituotannon
nimeke=Suojavarusteet {{!}} Sairaalatason suomalainen maskituotanto käynnistyi: ”Tuotantokoneet laulavat”
harhaanjohtavaa tekstiä: sanaa maski käytetään tavallisesti jokaisen käytettävissä olevasta suojasta ja hoitoammattilaisten suojista sanaa hengityssuojain
value.claim_en: In late May 2020, Finnish companies began producing hospital-grade masks, surgical masks, and respirators expected to cover domestic healthcare needs.
value.claim_fi: Toukokuun lopussa 2020 suomalaiset yritykset aloittivat sairaalatasoisten maskien, suu-nenäsuojusten ja hengityssuojainten tuotannon, jonka arvioitiin kattavan terveydenhuollon tarpeet.
value.uncertainty_note: Could also be classified as content_dispute over protective equipment terminology ('maski' vs. 'hengityssuojain'), since the editor was merely echoing the wording of mainstream news sources (Helsingin Sanomat), while also introducing minor typos ('keäkuusta', 'suu-nnäsuojusten') and punctuation errors.

value.what_changed_en: Added three unsourced sentences (plus a stray period) to the lead of the COVID-19 pandemic in Finland article, stating that the disease resembles a cold or flu in at least 80% of cases but is serious for those with weak immunity, that infection risk is elevated nationwide, and that some restrictions were lifted in April–May. The reverter removed it as unsourced despite being partly true.
evidence: Koronaviruksen aiheuttama sairaus on ainakin 80%:ssa tapauksista flunssaa muistuttava tauti, mutta niille joiden vastustuskyky sitä vastaan heikko, vakava sairaus.
Riski tartunnan saamiseen on kohonnut koko maassa.
Lähteetöntä, vaikka sinällään osin totta onkin
value.claim_en: COVID-19 is a cold-like illness in at least 80% of cases but severe for those with weak immunity against it, the infection risk is elevated across Finland, and some restrictions were lifted in April–May 2020.
value.claim_fi: Koronaviruksen aiheuttama tauti muistuttaa flunssaa ainakin 80 prosentissa tapauksista mutta on vakava heikon vastustuskyvyn omaaville, tartuntariski on kohonnut koko maassa ja joitain rajoituksia purettiin huhti–toukokuussa 2020.

value.what_changed_en: Broke the coat of arms image filename in the infobox and inserted a long string of incoherent Finnish words that resembles mobile predictive-text mashing.
evidence: alku ja loppu oli ihan ja se on on ollut 6B on on on on ja ja 6 on ollut
suuri kiitos paljon avusta en oo ole ei ei ei voi
value.uncertainty_note: Could also be viewed as deliberate vandalism (e.g. a school student mashing autocomplete—note '6B' which resembles a 6th-grade class name), though the text itself is pure gibberish.

value.what_changed_en: Added sourced details stating that Prime Minister Sanna Marin's use of the tax-free food benefit followed Prime Minister's Office (VNK) guidelines and that VNK later announced it would change those guidelines. The reverter undid it, noting the section had already been carefully negotiated and the addition brought nothing new.
evidence: Tuota kohtaa on hiottu jo aiemmin suuntaan jos toiseenkin, eikä maininta tuo aiempaan verrattuna mitään uutta tietoa.
value.claim_en: Sanna Marin's use of the tax-free food benefit followed the guidelines of the Prime Minister's Office, which subsequently announced it would change those guidelines.
value.claim_fi: Sanna Marinin elintarvike-edun käyttö oli valtioneuvoston kanslian ohjeen mukaista, ja valtioneuvoston kanslia ilmoitti sittemmin muuttavansa ohjetta.
value.narrative_en: Contextualising or defending Sanna Marin's actions in the breakfast benefit controversy
value.uncertainty_note: Could also be seen as a good_faith_error (redundant information already covered later in the paragraph beyond the context window) or mild pov_push (adding exculpatory framing to the opening sentence of a controversy), depending on what followed in the rest of the section.

value.what_changed_en: Added a sourced sentence about Kekkonen expressing antisemitic sentiments in letters home while lodging with a Jewish family in Germany in the early 1930s, including a derogatory quote ('never stay with a Jew if you can be among Christians'). The edit also introduced broken reference markup ('</ref.' and a stray '68'), and the reverter's summary ('Move to biography') indicates the detail was moved to a sub-article rather than rejected as false.
evidence: juutalaisvastaisuudesta | f | Mikähän tämä on? | viite-fix
Saksassa ollessaan Kekkonen asui ensin juutalaisen Rosenbaumin perheen luona, mikä sai hänet kirjoittamaan kotimaahan vastenmielisyydestään juutalaisia kohtaan
"ei koskaan jutin luo, jos saa kristittyjen parissa olla"
value.claim_en: While staying in Germany, Urho Kekkonen lived with the Jewish Rosenbaum family and wrote home expressing his dislike of Jews, stating after moving out that one should never stay with a Jew if one can be among Christians.
value.claim_fi: Saksassa ollessaan Urho Kekkonen asui juutalaisen Rosenbaumin perheen luona ja kirjoitti kotimaahan vastenmielisyydestään juutalaisia kohtaan todeten poismuuttonsa jälkeen, ettei koskaan pidä mennä juutalaisen luo, jos saa olla kristittyjen parissa.
value.uncertainty_note: The edit combines multiple consecutive revisions by the editor (as seen by '|'-separated summaries and messy leftover markup like '30–34' in removed_text vs context). Because the reverter removed it with 'Siirto elämäkertaan' (Move to biography sub-article), this could equally be classified as good_faith_error (misplaced detail / broken ref syntax) or content_dispute over due weight in the main article.

value.what_changed_en: Changed the estimated duration of the first wave of the COVID-19 epidemic from "two to three" months to "four to six" (with a typo, "neljöstö kuuteen") and added two new citations (from THL and Kauppalehti). However, the editor inserted the citations in the middle of the sentence before "kuukautta" (months) and left the previous conflicting citation intact at the end of the sentence, prompting a revert due to conflicting sources.
evidence: palautetaan, lähdekonflikti, tietolähteissä on erilaista tietoa, jota ei eritellä tekstissä
value.claim_en: The first wave of the coronavirus epidemic in Finland is estimated to last at least four to six months.
value.claim_fi: Ensimmäisen koronaepidemia-aallon arvioidaan Suomessa kestävän ainakin neljästä kuuteen kuukautta.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted Finnish vulgarities and slurs ('perseessä' meaning 'in the ass', 'paskottu' meaning 'shitted', 'homo' meaning 'gay') repeatedly inside existing words, broke citation and link markup, replaced 'Adolf Hitler' with gibberish ('laatu hillet'), and altered 'Moscow' ('Moskovan') to 'Ovamboland' ('ambomaan').

Added a sourced sentence (with a minor typo) to the article's lead section stating that critics favoring disease suppression argued the government's coronavirus models were overly optimistic and partly made in secret. It was reverted because the material was misplaced in the lead rather than the appropriate body section.
evidence: Taudin tukahduttamista knnattavien kriitikoiden mukaan hallituksen päätöksen pohjana käytettävät koronamallit olivat liian optimistisia ja osa niistä tehty salassa, ei avoimesti
ei oleellista johdantoon, teksti pitää sijoittaa oikeaan paikaan artikkelissa
value.claim_en: Critics advocating for disease suppression argued that the coronavirus models underlying the Finnish government's decisions were overly optimistic and partly created in secret rather than openly.
value.claim_fi: Taudin tukahduttamista kannattavien kriitikoiden mukaan Suomen hallituksen päätösten pohjana käytetyt koronamallit olivat liian optimistisia ja osittain salassa tehtyjä.
value.narrative_en: Criticism of the Finnish government's COVID-19 response and modelling transparency
value.uncertainty_note: Placing recent political criticism prominently in the lead section could also border on content_dispute (undue weight) or mild pov_push, though the reverter specifically treated it as a placement issue.

value.what_changed_en: Replaced a link to 'Serbia' with a link to 'Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes' (pointing to the article on the Kingdom of Yugoslavia) in the list of countries that recognized Finland's independence in 1922. The edit was reverted not for its content, which is historically accurate for 1922, but because it was identified as block evasion by a banned user ('eston kiertoa (WPK)').
evidence: Jugoslavian kuningaskunta|Serbien, kroaattien ja sloveenien kuningaskunta
value.claim_en: The Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, rather than Serbia, recognized Finland's independence in 1922.
value.claim_fi: Suomen itsenäistymisen tunnusti vuonna 1922 Serbien, kroaattien ja sloveenien kuningaskunta eikä Serbia.
value.uncertainty_note: The edit itself is a historically accurate correction (Serbia became part of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes in December 1918), though it changed cited text without checking how the cited source phrased it. It was reverted solely on procedural grounds for block evasion by a long-term banned editor ('WPK'), making 'other' fit better than 'good_faith_error'.

value.what_changed_en: Added a new section titled 'Next disease waves' summarizing contemporary Finnish news articles and expert predictions from summer 2020 about a potential second wave of COVID-19 and preparedness in Finland. It was reverted with the policy rationale 'Wikipedia does not predict' (WP:CRYSTAL).
evidence: Niinpä monet ennustivat Suomeenkin uutta tautiaaltoa.
Kriitikoiden mukaan Suomen varautuminen seuraavaan tautiaaltoon on puutteellista.
value.claim_en: In summer 2020, many experts predicted a potential second wave of COVID-19 in Finland that could be severe, while critics argued Finland's preparedness for it was inadequate.
value.claim_fi: Kesällä 2020 monet asiantuntijat ennustivat Suomeen mahdollista vakavaa toista korona-aaltoa, ja kriitikoiden mukaan Suomen varautuminen siihen oli puutteellista.
value.uncertainty_note: Could also be classified as a content_dispute over whether sourced contemporary expert predictions belong in an ongoing-event article, or mild pov_push due to synthesizing news commentary on government preparedness, though it includes both cautious and alarming viewpoints.

value.what_changed_en: In the 'Criticism' section, the editor added a sourced clause noting that former Prime Minister Jyrki Katainen had stated he used a similar grocery/meal service while living at the Kesäranta official residence. The reverter removed it on the grounds that similar comparisons to former PM Paavo Lipponen had already been removed earlier.
evidence: , joskin entinen pääministeri [[Jyrki Katainen]] on kertonut käyttäneensä vastaavaa palvelua asuessaan Kesärannassa.
Viittaukset Lipposiin poistettiin jo aiemmin, joten poistetaan myös Katainen
value.claim_en: Former Prime Minister Jyrki Katainen stated that he had used a similar state-funded grocery service while living at the Kesäranta official residence.
value.claim_fi: Entinen pääministeri Jyrki Katainen on kertonut käyttäneensä vastaavaa palvelua asuessaan Kesärannassa.
value.narrative_en: Contextualising Sanna Marin's Kesäranta breakfast allowance controversy by noting precedents by previous prime ministers
value.uncertainty_note: Could also be viewed as a mild pov_push (defending Marin via precedent) or good_faith_error (adding off-topic detail unaware of prior editorial consensus), though content_dispute best fits an editorial disagreement over scope and relevance of sourced context.

value.what_changed_en: The edit reverted an IP user's changes back to an earlier version, replacing terms like "Government" ("Hallitus"), "troops of the Republic of Finland", "rebels" ("kapinalliset"), and "October coup" with "White Senate" ("valkoinen senaatti"), "Whites", "Reds", and "October Revolution", while restoring a sourced summary paragraph.
evidence: Käyttäjän 85.76.x.x (keskustelu) muokkaukset kumottiin ja sivu palautettiin viimeisimpään käyttäjän 88.115.x.x tekemään versioon.
value.claim_en: The conflict in the Finnish Civil War was fought between the White Senate's forces and the Reds rather than between the official government's republican troops and rebels, and the 1917 Bolshevik takeover was a revolution rather than a coup.
value.claim_fi: Suomen sisällissodan osapuolina olivat valkoisen senaatin joukot ja punaiset eivätkä hallituksen alaiset tasavallan joukot ja kapinalliset, ja bolševikkien valtaannousu 1917 oli vallankumous eikä vallankaappaus.
value.narrative_en: Symmetrical civil war framing vs. legalist government-against-rebels framing
value.uncertainty_note: Because this edit is itself a revert between two IP editors' versions, it sits on the boundary between a sincere content_dispute over historiography/terminology and a pov_push; both versions reflect competing framings of the 1918 war in Finnish discussion.

value.what_changed_en: Added two unsourced sentences claiming that the Red Army did not provide any medical care to wounded prisoners of war at all, contrary to international agreements, and often shot them immediately. The edit was reverted for lacking sources ('Lähteetön').
evidence: Puna armeija ei kansainvälisien sopimuksien mukaan hoitanut ollenkaan haavoittuneita sotavankeja.
value.claim_en: The Red Army gave no medical care whatsoever to wounded prisoners of war during the Continuation War and often shot them immediately.
value.claim_fi: Puna-armeija ei hoitanut haavoittuneita sotavankeja lainkaan jatkosodan aikana, vaan heidät ammuttiin usein heti.
value.narrative_en: Emphasising Soviet war crimes and mistreatment of Finnish POWs
value.historical_note_en: While summary executions and severe neglect of wounded prisoners occurred on the frontline, the blanket claim that the Red Army gave no medical care at all is false, as wounded Finnish prisoners were also treated in Soviet field and camp hospitals (such as Cherepovets hospital camp).
value.uncertainty_note: The edit also carries a strong anti-Soviet slant and uses dehumanising grammar ('Ne' for people) alongside spelling errors, so 'pov_push' or 'good_faith_error' (repeating popular wartime lore without a source) are close alternatives.

value.what_changed_en: Inserted the mocking nickname "Hornet" (referencing an election controversy about F/A-18 Hornet fighter jets) into Sanna Marin's infobox and changed her title to "ex-prime minister"—including altering an official government citation title—immediately on the night of the 2023 parliamentary election while she was still in office.
evidence: Ex-pääministeri Sanna Marinin hallituksen ministerit Ex-pääministerin sijaisuusjärjestyksessä
value.claim_en: Sanna Marin is the former Prime Minister of Finland as of April 2, 2023.
value.claim_fi: Sanna Marin on Suomen entinen pääministeri 2. huhtikuuta 2023 alkaen.
value.narrative_en: Mockery of Sanna Marin following the 2023 Finnish parliamentary election
value.historical_note_en: Although Sanna Marin's party did not come first in the parliamentary election on April 2, 2023, she remained Prime Minister of Finland until Petteri Orpo's cabinet was appointed on June 20, 2023.
